articles.title_orig: Christa Pike still in critical condition after botched execution, lawyer says
articles.title_zh: Christa Pike still in critical condition after botched execution, lawyer says
articles.content_orig:
Media witnesses recount the moments before the execution of Christa Pike was halted in Nashville, Tenn., on Sept. 30, 2026.
Tennessee is reviewing its lethal injection process after a botched execution attempt left 50-year-old Christa Pike in critical condition.
Pike was receiving “lifesaving care” at a Nashville hospital on Thursday, having survived two shots of the lethal drug pentobarbital , her attorneys said in a press conference . It is the first time in the modern era of the U.S. death penalty that a person received lethal injection drugs and survived, according to the nonpartisan Death Penalty Information Center .
“This failed attempt is the worst we’ve ever seen and unlike any other botched execution in the modern era,” Robin Maher, the center’s director, said in a statement on Thursday.
Pike’s case has drawn scrutiny over the state’s decision to proceed with her execution, despite repeated warnings about its lethal injection protocol from her attorneys, who said she was subjected to “chemical torture.”
Gov. Bill Lee, a Republican, ordered an independent investigation of the lethal injection process late on Wednesday. Lee also suspended executions in the state till the end of the year, the second moratorium on executions during his time in office due to concerns over the state’s lethal injections.
“There is no one that wanted what happened last night to happen,” Lee told reporters on Thursday, describing the botched execution as a “tragedy.” But he stopped short of suggesting that he might heed renewed calls to commute Pike’s sentence to life in prison.
“The people of Tennessee have determined that the death penalty is the appropriate penalty for the most heinous crimes in the state,” Lee said. “The people of Tennessee make that decision, and my job is to make sure then that those sentences are carried out.”
Lee had denied Pike’s clemency request to commute her sentence to life in prison without the possibility of parole on Monday.
Pike, convicted of the 1995 murder of then-19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, has been on death row for more than 30 years. She would have been the first woman executed in Tennessee in more than 200 years. Only 18 women have been executed in the U.S. since 1976, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.
The Tennessee Department of Correction said in a statement to media outlets late Wednesday that it “had followed every step of the state’s lawful, established execution protocol approved by the attorney general’s office.” It described the lethal injection as “consistently effective.”
Lee defended the agency, saying it followed protocol.
TIME has reached out to the state’s Department of Correction and Pike’s attorneys for comment.
“There was no reason to expect it to not work,” Lee said. “But something didn’t go well or right last night, and we need to find out why.”
Randy Spivey, an attorney with the Tennessee Office of the Post-Conviction Defender, said Pike endured a “torturous” experience in the execution chamber. Pike’s left arm was pierced by at least seven needles, and her right arm turned purple, he said. She said her arm felt like it was “about to explode,” her attorneys said.
Pike’s attorneys suggested that the drugs may have entered her arm tissue instead of directly into her bloodstream. They described it as “chemical torture.”
Pike remained cooperative throughout the multiple execution attempts and tried to help her executioners, her attorneys said. “She over and over again said, ‘Please try up on my shoulder higher. Please try here. Please try here,’” Spivey said.
“We may never know what all she was suffering through, either because she can’t remember it, she can’t tell it, or it overwhelms her,” said Stephen Ferrell, from the Federal Defender Services of Eastern Tennessee. Pike’s greatest fear was not of dying but “of a prolonged, painful, traumatic death.”
“And that’s what happened,” Ferrell said. “Minus the death.”
Witnesses to the execution said late Wednesday that Pike could still be heard breathing and snoring an hour after her executioners administered two rounds of pentobarbital, including when the curtain closed and when witnesses were escorted out of the chamber.
Tennessee switched to a one-drug lethal injection of the barbiturate pentobarbital as its execution protocol in December 2024. Pike’s lawyers previously raised concerns about the source of the drugs, while Reuters reported on Thursday that that information had been withheld. E.U. law bars pharmaceutical companies from selling drugs for use in executions, leading some U.S. prison systems to procure the drugs from compounding pharmacies in processes often shielded by state secrecy laws.
In legal filings , Pike’s lawyers had raised concerns that Pike’s execution by lethal injection might be compromised by her small veins and medical history of thrombocytosis. But their petitions to the state to use alternative execution methods, like death by hanging, were denied.
Pike’s lawyers said in a statement that their concerns proved true: “difficult vein access, blown veins, degraded pentobarbital, no emergency medical care available when things inevitably go wrong, all under a protocol that remains veiled in secrecy.”
In a June court filing , Pike’s attorneys pointed to the state’s failed execution of Tony Carruthers in May, when medical staff failed to find a vein. Lee granted Carruthers a one-year reprieve.
The American Medical Association and American Nurses Association prohibit doctors and nurses from participating in executions under their professional ethics standards. Some states have used execution personnel without current medical licenses. Tennessee, however, requires the participation of physicians, or other medically trained personnel in an execution.
After the botched execution of Carruthers, more than 40 doctors and nurses penned a letter to Lee, calling on him to redesign the protocol to exclude health care workers, arguing that it is at odds with their commitment to preserve life.
Lee also paused executions and ordered an independent review in 2022 after it was discovered that prison officials failed to properly test lethal injection drugs for endotoxins in the lead-up to the planned execution of Oscar Franklin Smith. Smith was ultimately killed in May 2025, three years after Lee issued a temporary reprieve.
The review resulted in the one-drug protocol that was used on Wednesday. It also showed that officials had skipped proper endotoxin testing for multiple prior executions.
Pike’s attorneys have publicly called on the state’s governor to reconsider commuting Pike’s sentence to life in prison. Pike, who was sentenced in March 1996 at age 20, has expressed remorse for the torture and murder of her classmate. Her legal team had asked courts to review mitigating claims of sexual abuse and rape as a child, which they said Tennessee had disputed in earlier proceedings. They also separately argued that aspects of the execution process could trigger PTSD related to that abuse, constituting cruel and unusual punishment.
Hours before the scheduled execution on Wednesday, a federal appeals court issued an eleventh hour stay of execution to review the case. The state asked the Supreme Court to vacate the lower court’s ruling, which it did in a 6-3 decision , allowing Tennessee officials to proceed. The Supreme Court did not explain its decision.
In her dissent alongside liberal justices Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson, Justice Sonia Sotomayor wrote, “I see no reason to short-circuit the ordinary process of appellate review, particularly in light of the grave consequences of an erroneous decision. Tennessee’s desire to expedite Pike’s execution by a few days or even weeks cannot outweigh her ‘fundamental interest in [her] own life.’”
Pike’s underlying case remains pending before the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit.
Pike’s case has also renewed calls to abolish the death penalty.

articles.title_orig: Green Party members back 'Zionism is racism' motion
articles.title_zh: Green Party members back 'Zionism is racism' motion
articles.content_orig:
Israel called the motion a ‘twisted resolution’. The Green Party, led by Zack Polanksi, has 5 MPs in Britain’s 650-seat parliament
The UK’s left-wing Green Party on Sunday voted to define Zionism as racism at the party’s annual meeting, drawing sharp backlash from British Jewish groups and the Israeli government.
Members of the Green Party, which has five MPs in Britain’s 650-seat parliament and which enjoyed a boost in recent local and special elections, backed the motion at the party’s conference, with 1,022 votes in favour and 813 against.
According to the motion, Zionism would be “treated as any other form of racism” and the party supports the establishment of a “single democratic Palestinian State in all of historic Palestine”.
“This has been a serious and deeply felt debate within our membership,” a Green spokesperson said.

articles.title_orig: Polls close in Brazil as country awaits results of high-stakes election
articles.title_zh: Polls close in Brazil as country awaits results of high-stakes election
articles.content_orig:
Polls have closed in Brazil's general election, after voters queued in long lines for a tight first round of the presidential race.
After casting his ballot, 80-year-old left-wing President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva warned that the choice was between democracy and "barbarism".
His challenger, right-winger Flávio Bolsonaro, 45, said he wanted to "free the Brazilian people".
The result is forecast to be close. BBC Brazil's poll aggregator shows that the gap between Lula and Bolsonaro is only two points. If no candidate gets more than 50% of the vote, the election will go to a run-off on 25 October.
According to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court (TSE), more than 158.7 million Brazilians, including one million people abroad, are eligible to vote in the election.
Lula is challenged by 11 candidates, although BBC Brazil's poll aggregator shows that candidates other than Lula and Bolsonaro will get only about 10% of the vote.
The TSE has not set a fixed time for the release of the official results, but they are expected within hours because voting is electronic and experience from previous elections shows that results tend to come quickly.
A victory for Bolsonaro would extend a wave of wins across Latin America by right-wing candidates aligned with US President Donald Trump, while Lula's re-election would create problems for Washington, which has clashed with his government over trade and security.
Some countries, from which Brazilians living overseas are able to vote, have already released preliminary vote count data.
In China, Lula won 56.63% of the votes, while Bolsonaro came in second with 31.33%. Lula also won in countries including South Korea, New Zealand and Saudi Arabia.
In Israel, however, Bolsonaro won 74.40% of the valid votes. He also won 71.59% of the valid votes in Japan.
Today's result will also determine the composition of the Senate from February 2027 onwards, as 54 of the Senate's 81 seats are being contested, representing two-thirds of the chamber.
Currently, the largest bloc in the Senate is Bolsonaro's Liberal Party (PL), followed by the Social Democratic Party (PSD), which has served in a coalition government under Lula.
In the last election four years ago, Lula narrowly defeated Flávio Bolsonaro's father, Jair. But the tumultuous aftermath of the election, which saw Jair Bolsonaro convicted of plotting a coup after thousands of his supporters stormed the Brazilian Congress, has had a lasting impact on the nation's political life and this election.
Jair Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup and is barred from standing for office.
Because of recurrent health problems, he is currently under house arrest rather than in a cell, but he has been prohibited from posting on social media or making public statements.
Despite these restrictions, there is little doubt that Flávio Bolsonaro has his father's backing.

articles.title_orig: Team Champions in the Sprint Cup: Team WRT wins another title in GT World Challenge Europe.
articles.title_zh: Team Champions in the Sprint Cup: Team WRT wins another title in GT World Challenge Europe.
articles.content_orig:
Laura Claesgens BMW Group Tel: +49-151-601-47299 send an e-mail
Barcelona. Team WRT has secured another title in the GT World
    Challenge Europe powered by AWS with its BMW M4 GT3 EVOs. In the
    final Sprint Cup races of the year at Barcelona (ESP), the Belgian
    team won the Sprint Cup Teams’ classification. It is Team WRT’s
    fourth title of the year in this championship, after it had already
    secured the Sprint, Endurance and Combined titles in the Silver Cup
    early. Strong comebacks by the team’s BMW M4 GT3 EVOs in both races
    laid the foundation for the latest title success. Team WRT also won
    the Pitstop Challenge for the best pit crew. KPX Motorsport also had
    reason to celebrate with a Gold Cup podium on Saturday.
The first qualifying session on Saturday morning proved difficult for
  the BMW teams. Race one in the afternoon, which was marked by heavy
  rain and numerous spins and accidents, had to be interrupted with a
  red flag halfway through. David Pittard (GBR) and Jop Rappange (NED)
  made a fantastic comeback in the KPX Motorsport #77 BMW M4 GT3 EVO,
  climbing from the back of the grid to eighth overall. At the same
  time, they secured second place on the Gold Cup podium.
The Team WRT PRO Cup cars also worked their way forward from the back
  of the grid. Kelvin van der Linde (RSA) and Charles Weerts (BEL)
  finished tenth in the #32 car, followed by car #31 of Jordan Pepper
  (RSA) and Amaury Cordeel (BEL) in eleventh. Valentino Rossi (ITA) and
  Max Hesse (GER) brought the #46 car home in 16th place. On Saturday
  evening, the authorities issued severe weather warnings for the
  region, forecasting extreme heavy rain through Sunday afternoon. The
  schedule was changed accordingly with the second qualifying session
  being cancelled and race two postponed until Sunday evening. The grid
  was based on times from Friday’s second free practice session. The
  highest-placed BMW M4 GT3 EVO was the #46 car in 15th on the grid.
Race two was held in dry and excellent conditions. Van der Linde
  gained no fewer than 15 positions during the chaotic opening stage
  alone. He and Weerts continued to move further up the field as the
  race progressed, eventually bringing the #32 car home in sixth place.
  Pepper and Cordeel also made a strong comeback in car #31, this time
  climbing as high as eighth. Hesse and Rossi were also on course for a
  top-ten finish in the #46 car, but then the driver’s door came loose
  and Rossi had to pit for an unscheduled repair stop. They eventually
  finished 38th.
Three-time Silver Cup champions Matisse Lismont (BEL) and Ignacio
  Montenegro (ARG) finished seventh in class on Saturday with the #30
  BMW M4 GT3 EVO of Team WRT. On Sunday, Lismont was hit at the start
  and the duo had to retire from the race. In the Bronze Cup, BMW M
  works driver Augusto Farfus (BRA) again shared the #991 BMW M4 GT3 EVO
  of Paradine Competition with Darren Leung (GBR). The duo finished
  fourth in class in both races.
The 2026 season in the GT World Challenge Europe powered by AWS will
  conclude in two weeks’ time, on 17 October, with a final Endurance
  race at Portimão (POR).
Reactions after the races at Barcelona:
Vincent Vosse, Team Principal Team WRT: “I am
  delighted and proud of the team. The Sprint Cup is a championship that
  is particularly close to our hearts. In our 14 participations, we have
  now won the title for the twelfth time. A big thank you to everyone
  who contributed to this achievement. Winning the Pitstop Challenge is
  also something very special. Bravo to all the mechanics for their
  great work. They really deliver something extraordinary. We also saw
  in Barcelona how important pit stops are for making up positions. Now
  we are looking forward to Portimão.”
Kelvin van der Linde (#32 BMW M4 GT3 EVO, Team WRT, Race 1:
    10th place, Race 2: 6th place): “I am very happy for the
  team. They really deserved it, even though the past three weekends
  have been very difficult for us in terms of performance. We always
  stuck together, and I am very pleased that we were still able to win
  the Teams’ Championship today. That was a top race: top strategy, top
  pit stops – everything just came together, and we had a little bit of
  luck on our side as well.”
Jordan Pepper (#31 BMW M4 GT3 EVO, Team WRT, Race 1: 11th
    place, Race 2: 8th place): “Obviously we came into this
  year trying to fight for a championship on the drivers’ side but we
  just didn’t have a season that came together. Still, I’m really proud
  because, across the three pro cars, we were able to win the team
  championship. That’s important, because there’s such a big group of
  people here working from the beginning of winter through all the test
  programmes and long days. To reward them with that is impressive, and
  I’m really proud of them. On top of that, there are some other
  internal championships we were able to win, like the Pitstop
  Challenge, which was incredible from our guys. What we showed this
  weekend, when we didn’t have the necessary pace, was that by executing
  all the other factors perfectly, we were able to move to the front.
  That’s really impressive, and we showed that we can work as a team.”
Max Hesse (#46 BMW M4 GT3 EVO, Team WRT, Race 1: 16th place,
    Race 2: 38th place): “I’m very happy that the team won the
  championship and also the Pitstop Challenge. They deserved it. We in
  the #46 car also contributed a little bit here and there, so we can be
  happy with that. Unfortunately, our Barcelona weekend was difficult,
  and a lot went against us, but we never gave up, kept fighting and had
  good pace in the second race. We’ll take that with us to Portimão, and
  we’ll attack again there.”
Munich, 13 May 2026. Watch the webcast of the public session of the 106th Annual General Meeting of BMW AG.

articles.title_orig: Beyond mining tunnels: China's coal-rich province accelerates smarter, greener energy transition
articles.title_zh: Beyond mining tunnels: China's coal-rich province accelerates smarter, greener energy transition
articles.content_orig:
This photo taken on Sept. 4, 2026 shows a view outside the main venue of the 2026 Taiyuan Energy Low-Carbon Development Forum in Taiyuan, north China's Shanxi Province. (Xinhua/Yang Chenguang)
TAIYUAN, Oct. 3 (Xinhua) -- From intelligent coal mines to digital power-grid management, north China's Shanxi Province is accelerating its energy transition and maintaining stable coal supplies.
As one of China's major coal-producing provinces and a key national energy base, Shanxi is seeking to make its energy system smarter, more diversified and more efficient.
The province is upgrading its traditional coal industry through smarter technologies and cleaner production, while expanding wind and solar power to diversify its energy mix. Backed by increasingly flexible power management, these efforts are reshaping how Shanxi produces, supplies and uses energy as China pursues greener development.
For 50-year-old Zhao Huacheng, deputy head of a fully mechanized mining team at Huayang New Material Technology Group Co., Ltd., a major coal mining enterprise in Shanxi, the transformation of coal mining is evident in his daily work.
Zhao has worked in the industry for nearly 30 years, taking on almost every frontline role in his team, from coal miner and powered-support operator to safety officer.
Huayang's No. 1 Mine, with an annual production capacity of 8.5 million tonnes, is among China's first batch of intelligent demonstration coal mines. Its intelligent mining faces use 5G technology and automated equipment to enable remote control and reduce the need for underground workers.
The number of workers required underground for a shift at Zhao's team has already fallen from 24 to 16.
Operating a coal-cutting machine was once one of the toughest jobs. Three operators had to work together, with one controlling the machine from a platform and the other two observing the terrain from the front and rear.
When the machine started up, clouds of coal dust often made it nearly impossible to see, and flying chunks of coal posed a real risk of injury. Zhao still has a scar near his right eye as a reminder.
"With advances in technology, the operator in the middle is no longer needed. The operators in front and behind can control the machine remotely from six meters away, reducing the risks," Zhao said. "We used to get bumped and bruised almost constantly. Now, such incidents are rare."
Today, intelligent equipment has taken over most labor-intensive tasks. Clean mine tunnels, dust-suppression systems and enclosed control rooms have replaced the once dusty and hazardous working conditions.
Productivity has also seen a sharp increase. A production shift that once yielded about 3,000 to 4,000 tonnes of coal can now produce 5,000 to 6,000 tonnes, according to Zhao.
The transformation at Zhao's workplace is part of a broader push to make coal mining smarter and cleaner in Shanxi. By the end of November 2025, the province had built 369 intelligent coal mines, accounting for more than one-third of the national total, as well as 75 demonstration mines for green mining.
On the national level, China aims to make virtually all types of coal mines intelligent by 2035 by leveraging advanced technologies, according to the National Development and Reform Commission.
While making coal production smarter and cleaner, Shanxi is also reshaping its energy mix, with renewable energy becoming an increasingly important source of new capacity and power generation.
At Shanxi Jinnan Steel Group Co., Ltd. in Quwo County, Linfen City, photovoltaic panels cover unused spaces ranging from rooftops and south-facing walls to hillside slopes and areas near an artificial lake.
The company produces nearly 6 million tonnes of steel annually. Over the past five years, it has invested heavily in clean energy projects to reduce the carbon intensity of its energy consumption.
Three months ago, the company partnered with PowerChina New Energy Group Co., Ltd. to develop green electricity by tapping the region's mountainous and valley resources. The two sides plan to use a "green electricity direct supply" model to better match the company's energy needs.
"We have developed photovoltaic projects with a combined capacity of 550 megawatts, generating more than 1 billion kWh of electricity annually," said Zhang Tianfu, president of Shanxi Jinnan Steel Group Co., Ltd.
Green electricity currently accounts for 15 percent of the company's power consumption. Zhang said the company will continue expanding its renewable energy portfolio and plans to raise the share to 50 percent by 2029.
The company's growing investment in green electricity comes as renewable energy has become the main source of newly added power generation capacity and electricity generation in Shanxi.
By the end of June this year, the province's installed capacity of wind and solar power had exceeded 80 million kW. In 2020, roughly one in every seven kWh generated in Shanxi came from renewable sources. Today, despite a substantial increase in total power generation, the share has risen to one in every four kWh.
A historic shift has taken place in Shanxi's energy mix. By the end of September last year, installed capacity of new and clean energy sources accounted for 54.55 percent of the province's total, marking a historic shift from a fossil-fuel-dominated energy mix toward one led by clean energy.
As wind and solar power generation expands, Shanxi faces a new challenge: how to accommodate increasingly variable renewable generation while keeping the power grid stable.
Virtual power plants are emerging as one solution.
Shanxi Fengxingcekong Co., Ltd. operates China's first virtual power plant participating in the electricity spot market. Nan Dou, deputy general manager of the company, said the spot market generates a new electricity price every five minutes.
The virtual power plant aggregates scattered electricity-consuming resources and dispatches them through a digital platform, using algorithms to adjust the power loads of participating enterprises in response to changes in electricity prices and grid demand.
"When electricity prices are low and renewable power generation is high, we encourage enterprises to consume more electricity, maximizing the use of renewable power. When prices are high and the grid is under pressure, we organize enterprises to reduce their loads during peak periods, helping ensure safe and stable grid operation," Nan said.
"This benefits all three sides by ensuring power supplies, facilitating renewable power consumption and reducing energy costs for enterprises," he added.
From August 2023 to June 2026, the virtual power plant helped facilitate the consumption of 350 million kWh of renewable electricity, equivalent to reducing carbon dioxide emissions by about 350,000 tonnes, the operators said. It also saved about 210 million kWh of electricity.
Over the three years since entering the electricity market, the company's ability to aggregate and dispatch resources has continued to improve. The number of users on its platform has risen from five to more than 60, while its aggregated capacity has jumped from 80,000 kW to 2.282 million kW.
"The most important improvement is that our control success rate has risen from 33 percent to 80 percent. Only by improving the quality of regulation can we achieve the desired results," Nan said.
As of September 2026, 14 virtual power plants in Shanxi had participated in market trading, aggregating 1,459 users. Their combined capacity in the Shanxi electricity market had reached 6.4548 million kW, with a maximum adjustable load of 1.545 million kW.
Traditional coal-fired power plants are also undergoing flexibility upgrades in response to market signals. The upgrades allow them to reduce output when wind and solar generation is abundant, creating more room for renewable power, and quickly ramp up output when renewable generation falls short, helping ensure electricity supplies.

articles.title_zh: China upholds principles, promotes dialogue at G20 trade ministers' meeting: commerce ministry
articles.content_orig:
China played an active role in promoting dialogue and cooperation with other G20 members while upholding principles during the recent G20 trade ministers’ meeting, the country’s Ministry of Commerce said on Sunday.
The ministry spokesperson made the remarks in response to a media question about the meeting, which was held on Sept. 30 and Oct. 1 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, the United States.
Members exchanged views on issues proposed by the U.S. G20 presidency, including opposing the weaponization of food, addressing overcapacity, eliminating forced labor, and adjusting the Most-Favored-Nation (MFN) principle.
Members reached a joint statement opposing the weaponization of food, while no outcome documents were issued on the remaining matters, according to the ministry.
During the meeting, the Chinese side consistently upheld an attitude of openness and cooperation, constructively participated in discussions and maintained close communication with other members, fully playing its role in promoting dialogue and cooperation, said the spokesperson.
At the same time, China adhered to its principles, resolutely safeguarded the common interests of China and other developing countries, and worked to promote unity and cooperation within the G20, the ministry added.
Regarding the food issue, many emerging markets and developing members, including China, put forward the view that food-importing and food-exporting countries should jointly safeguard the stability of food supply chains, and that all parties have the right to take measures for domestic public policy objectives and to safeguard food security, the spokesperson said.
The presidency gave positive consideration to these views, which were also fully reflected in the joint statement, the spokesperson said, adding that the outcome was the result of consensus-building and the joint efforts of all G20 members.
Issues such as overcapacity and forced labor were highly controversial from the outset, said the ministry. The ministry said that at present, G20 members are generally subject to additional Section 301 tariffs under the pretext of so-called “forced labor” and are mostly targets of Section 301 investigations over the so-called “overcapacity” issue.
Against this backdrop, many members put forward different views on the issues set by the presidency, and the meeting ultimately failed to produce outcome documents on these matters, the ministry said.
The spokesperson also noted that, after the meeting, the U.S. side issued a chair’s statement mentioning that it had released a statement on forced labor with two other G20 countries outside the G20 framework.
On the issue of reforming the MFN treatment principle, the vast majority of members, including China, emphasized that the principle is the cornerstone of the multilateral trading system, providing stability and predictability for global trade, and that any undermining of this principle would seriously damage the foundation of the multilateral trading system, said the ministry.
In light of the views expressed by the members, the presidency did not propose an outcome document on this topic, the ministry revealed.
Looking ahead to the G20 Leaders’ Summit in December 2026, the spokesperson said that China is ready to work with the G20 presidency and all members to uphold consensus-building, and jointly contribute positive and practical economic and trade outcomes to the summit.

articles.title_orig: Some climb for faith, others for the views. This Chinese sacred mountain draws them all
articles.title_zh: Some climb for faith, others for the views. This Chinese sacred mountain draws them all
articles.content_orig:
WUDANG, China (AP) — A banknote clasped between her hands, Liu Haiyan prayed to the protector of the Wudang mountains. The range in central China has long been considered sacred in Taoism .
“I asked him to bless our motherland with favorable weather and to make it even more prosperous,” Liu said while sitting outside the Golden Hall, a Taoist temple at the summit of Tianzhu Peak.
“This place watches over our country,” she added. “We’re Chinese and this is part of our faith.”
Tourists and pilgrims in a steady stream make their way through Wudang every day. Its scenic peaks, ancient palaces and religious sites drew 14 million visits in 2025, according to government figures.
Wudang’s Taoist buildings date as far back as the 7th century. The complex expanded over centuries through China’s Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties.
Liu traveled several hundred kilometers (miles) from Hebei province with her daughter, Ji Jiaxin. She also prayed to Wudang’s protector, known as Zhenwu.
“He can guide people toward goodness,” Ji said. “He also watches over all the living things that grow across the land.”
Both women see Wudang as a place of scenic beauty and spiritual significance. Perched at about 1,610 meters (5,280 feet) above sea level, the Golden Hall is a place where they experience a sense of spiritual purification.
“Everyone comes here with a sincere heart,” Liu said. “With sincerity, the divine will respond.”
The Wudang mountain range comprises 72 peaks, all thought to converge toward Tianzhu. Its lower slopes are associated with fire, while the deity enshrined at its summit is linked to water.
“Water at the top can moisten the earth, while fire below provides warmth and enables all living things to grow,” said Shu Chenghai, director of social education at Wudang Museum.
The Golden Hall’s construction reflects this symbolism too.
In the traditional Chinese concept of the Five Elements, metal is believed to generate water. And since natural sources can run dry over time, the bronze hall serves as a means to nourish Heaven and Earth.
“It embodies prayers for favorable weather, abundant harvests and peace and prosperity throughout the country,” Shu said.
Taoist priests and monks look after the religious sites throughout Wudang. With their hair tied in high buns and dressed in distinctive blue robes, they glide through the temples, talking to visitors and scanning tickets at the entrances.
Their role also connects Wudang’s spiritual life with the communities that call the mountain home.
Cai Hongping was born in the area. Her family settled beside Zixiao Palace, a major Taoist temple complex.
“Some of the elderly Taoist priests there were exceptionally kind and compassionate,” Cai said. “Sometimes they gave us dates, peanuts or fruit.”
Life in the mountains was difficult when Cai was a child. Food and other material goods were scarce, but she remembers the temples as places of happiness and joy.
“I often went with the Taoist priests to identify Chinese medicinal herbs, practiced martial arts with them, and sometimes stole fruit that had been left as offerings,” Cai said.
Her connection to the mountain extended beyond its temples.
Cai’s grandfather was a heritage conservation worker in Wudang, a role focused on preserving and cataloging cultural relics. Her father also made walking sticks for visitors. Cai and other relatives sometimes joined him in gathering medicinal herbs to sell.
“The entire mountain was my childhood,” Cai said. “It has also given me a reverence for life.”
Wudang’s palaces and temples flourished during the Ming dynasty, when Emperor Zhu Di undertook a major building campaign to align his imperial regime with Taoism.
At its height, the complex included dozens of temples, palaces and monasteries. More than 60 sites survive today.
Wudang’s development coincided with another major project commissioned by Zhu Di: the Forbidden City in Beijing.
“When we say, ‘The Forbidden City was built in the north, and Wudang was developed in the south,’ we mean that these two World Cultural Heritage sites are like twins,” Shu said.
“The two places conveyed a message to the world: one represented Heaven, while the other represented the human realm,” he added.
Wudang’s special connection with Ming dynasty emperors remains visible today.
Along the route taken by tourists and pilgrims are several steles marking ritual proclamations made on behalf of emperors during the first year of each reign.
“An emperor needed to make a ritual proclamation to Zhenwu,” Shu said. “He would declare that he had succeeded to the imperial throne and express his hope for Heaven’s support.”
Long before today’s visitors made their way to Wudang, the mountain drew people seeking solitude and spiritual cultivation.
Shu said its distinctive landscape embodies the traditional Chinese concept of “Dong Tian Fu Di,” or “grotto-heavens and blessed lands” — places traditionally regarded as sacred retreats.
“The idea is that a profound harmony between humanity and nature is not merely something human beings can create,” he added.
Beyond the Golden Hall, visitors encounter other temples and figures associated with different needs, from health and inner balance to martial arts.
Wang Xia recently traveled from Inner Mongolia and visited Taizipo, or Prince Slope, a Taoist temple complex linked to Zhenwu’s legendary early life as a prince.
“The fact that the crown prince once studied here makes it particularly appealing,” Wang said. “I wanted to pray for my child, to wish her academic success and a bright future.”
Her first encounter with Wudang came from books. She read about the Ming dynasty and began to dream about visiting the site herself one day.
“I imagined that coming here would give me the feeling of entering the world of Taoist immortals,” Wang said. “That is what this place feels like: a mountain of immortals.”
AP video journalist Wu Jia contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: How was Flydubai co-pilot cleared despite being deemed a security risk?
articles.title_zh: How was Flydubai co-pilot cleared despite being deemed a security risk?
articles.content_orig:
A Flydubai co-pilot accused of attacking his captain with an emergency axe and attempting to seize control of the flight bound for Israel had previously been barred from flying over concerns about alleged “extremist” views, raising questions about how he was allowed to fly to Tel Aviv.
The co-pilot has been identified as Hamam al-Hammami, an Omani national, according to multiple media reports.
The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has described the September 30 incident aboard Flight FZ1073 as an attempted “terrorist” operation .
But investigators are still working to establish the motive and whether anyone else was connected to the attack, which has raised concerns about pilot vetting and aviation security.
So, what security checks do pilots have to go through and how al-Hammami may have evaded background checks?
That is now one of the central questions facing investigators.
Al-Hammami had previously been barred from flying in Oman because of concerns that he had adopted “extremist” views and was instead moved to an administrative role at Oman Air, according to sources who spoke to the AP news agency.
He was subsequently hired by Flydubai.
A Gulf diplomat told AP that al-Hammami had undergone standard security checks before being hired. It wasn’t immediately clear to what extent the co-pilot was vetted.
The US-based network CNN reported that a LinkedIn profile bearing al-Hammami’s name said he had spent seven years at Oman Air before leaving in February 2025. The profile said he joined Royal Air Maroc in June 2025 and left in January this year.
It is unclear what those alleged views were or whether Oman informed other countries or airlines about its concerns.
Background checks for commercial pilots vary by airline and country, with no single global standard governing the process, an airline pilot and instructor told Al Jazeera.
The captain with an international airline who chose to remain anonymous said pilots are generally required to obtain aviation medical certification from the regulator in the country where they are licensed to fly.
In the UAE, that is overseen by the General Civil Aviation Authority (GCAA), he said.
Some airlines also require prospective pilots to provide police clearance certificates from their country of residence as part of pre-employment screening, the pilot added.
One type of check is a Class 1 medical assessment, which typically examines areas including vision, hearing, cardiovascular and neurological health, as well as conditions that could cause sudden incapacitation.
When it comes to security checks, aviation rules require background checks for personnel who have unescorted access to security-restricted areas.
Psychological assessments, drug and alcohol testing and other evaluations may be required depending on the jurisdiction.
Israel has some of the world’s toughest aviation security measures.
As a result, questions have been raised over how the alleged attacker was allowed to operate a flight to Israel, despite reportedly being an Omani national and Oman having no diplomatic relations with Israel.
According to the Haaretz newspaper, Israeli authorities received the Flydubai flight’s crew and passenger lists before it departed. Under a law passed in 2023, airlines are required to provide information about passengers and crew members, including their names and nationalities, to Israel up to 48 hours before a flight.
The Israel Tax Authority confirmed to Haaretz that it had received the lists for the Flydubai flight. The media outlet reported that the information is also supposed to be available to Israeli security bodies, including the Mossad, police and Shin Bet, to identify people who may pose a security risk.
According to security sources who spoke to Haaretz, the Transportation Ministry’s Security Department and the Mossad are responsible for checking foreign flight crews and issuing alerts if concerns arise.
However, two security sources told Haaretz that while the Transportation Ministry holds responsibility “on paper”, it does not have its own intelligence capacity.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has said that Israel has longstanding arrangements with foreign airlines aimed at preventing pilots who are nationals of countries without diplomatic relations with Israel from flying there.
Netanyahu has described what happened as a “loophole” and Israel says it will now strengthen its checks.
The UAE has not yet publicly established a motive or announced whether investigators believe al-Hammami acted alone.
UAE presidential adviser Anwar Gargash said on Saturday that the latest ‘terrorist’ attack is a new warning that the region’s fight against “extremism” is not over.
“This underscores the importance of the UAE’s early and firm stance: no tolerance for extremism and no leniency towards its rhetoric. Security begins with confronting hatred and drying up the sources of extremism,” he posted on X.

articles.title_orig: Beyond the Moon: Space Week around the world
articles.title_zh: Beyond the Moon: Space Week around the world
articles.content_orig:
Facebook Twitter Print Email
Right after the Soviet Union launched Sputnik in 1957, UNOOSA , the UN Office for Outer Space Affairs, was established and has since been monitoring developments across more than 77 successful lunar missions and other journeys while also taking a lead role in the annual World Space Week , which runs from 4 to 10 October.
Early this year, the UN hosted four astronauts who just returned from outer space , carrying out the farthest human spaceflight in history when they travelled beyond the far side of the Moon.
But, the UN has been involved in space affairs for decades. The General Assembly created a committee in 1959 to govern the exploration and use of space for the benefit of all – focused around peace, security and development.
Instrumental in creating the five treaties and principles governing outer space, the Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space (COPUOS) has mandated duties that include keeping pace with rapid technological advances.
Since then, space science and technology and their applications are increasingly being used to support a wide range of UN activities. At least 25 UN entities use them.
Cosmic crops : The International Atomic Energy Agency ( IAEA ) and the Food and Agriculture Organization ( FAO ) sent seeds to the International Space Station in November 2022 to test how harsh space conditions alter plant genetics for climate resilience on Earth
Satellite tele-medicine : The World Health Organization ( WHO ) collaborated with UNOOSA to apply space science and satellite technology to help solve global health challenges
Space junk : The UN Environment Programme ( UNEP ) helps to promote long-term sustainability in Earth’s orbit given the 130 million pieces of debris in circulation – from satellite fragments to abandoned spacecraft
“Like entering a dream state,” one astronaut recalled.
In 1990, 17 astronauts shared their out-of-this-world experiences in Our Planet Earth , a timeless documentary produced for the UN by Lemle Pictures, Inc. with cooperation of the Association for Space Explorers and the Canadian International Development Agency.
“It was the greatest feeling I ever had in my entire life,” said one astronaut. “Seeing the black sky and the bright sun. This is really impossible, but I saw it.”
Another said he tried clumsily manoeuvring in a state of weightlessness, finding himself awkwardly jammed against a window when he was awestruck by both the view and the magnificence of Earth.
One summed up a commonly shared feeling among the space travellers.
“I felt a love for all the inhabitants of the Earth,” he said. “I just wanted to love them all.”

articles.title_orig: Minecraft Dungeons II Reviews Praise Local Co-Op but Fault the Open World
articles.title_zh: Minecraft Dungeons II Reviews Praise Local Co-Op but Fault the Open World
articles.content_orig:
Nintendo Life called Minecraft Dungeons II a fun but flawed sequel in its Switch 2 review, with co-operative play as the high point. A second review, from Shacknews , reached a similar verdict and said the game works best with friends sitting in the same room.
The game follows Minecraft Dungeons, which came out in 2020 as a loot-driven dungeon crawler. Families who play together on one console are the audience both reviewers had in mind.
Nintendo Life said the sequel swaps the first game's episodic progression for an open world. Its reviewer said developer Mojang stretched the appeal too thin in doing so.
Dungeons are scattered across the Overworld, and portals lead to a new biome called The Sift, which the review found lovely to look at.
The story picks up after the first game. An Illager High Council, a trio of magic users wielding soul power, invades the land, and the player's custom hero starts in the hub town of Brave Haven.
Nintendo Life put the main campaign at about 12 to 15 hours and said it is easy.
Nintendo Life said customisation remains the strongest part of the game. Loot drops steadily from enemies and chests, and all weapons and gear can be enchanted.
Artefacts grant up to three crowd-control abilities in exchange for soul power, while Talismans are new and add stat boosts and resistances. Jumping now adds variety to melee and ranged attacks.
The reviewer wrote that players mostly use those builds against the same enemies in similar-looking locations. Endermen, which appear as random encounters, were singled out as a tense source of good gear.
Shacknews writer Ozzie Mejia said he mostly played online and found it frustrating for several reasons. He enjoyed offline play with friends and family far more.
Players must choose online or offline when they create a character, and the choice cannot be reversed. A hero built for online sessions cannot be moved to a living-room game, so a new character is required.
Both modes allow players to join and leave mid-game, and online players can connect through party codes or matchmaking.
Mejia described the storytelling as minimalistic. The game has few cutscenes and almost no voiceover beyond some narration, and it leans on text.
He said the cutscenes look gorgeous in Unreal Engine 5, and that the narrated quest text reminded him of a Dungeons & Dragons campaign. He said the format grew on him by the end.
Shacknews said the sequel keeps the first game's simple loop while adding depth drawn from the Minecraft source material. Mojang developed the game with Double Eleven.
I cover what the internet is actually talking about: the new release, the viral moment, the creator beef, the product launch. My job is to explain it fast and clearly, without the breathless hype. I read the timeline…

articles.title_orig: -60 kg: Ahmad Yusifov is Azerbaijan’s New Hero
articles.title_zh: -60 kg: Ahmad Yusifov is Azerbaijan’s New Hero
articles.content_orig:
Judo is always an amazing sport to watch or take part in, one that provides challenge, not just from fighter to fighter, but in our thinking and analysis. This category challenged the established order in Baku, yielding an immensely exciting day of judo.
As the judoka entered the arena, the volume rose ten-fold! Ahmad Yusifov had already given his crowd much to be thankful for and they were determined to continue giving their support right until the end. Sherzod Davlatov, however, had no intention of buckling under the pressure of Yusifov’s home-ground advantage.
Davlatov arrived with a powerful style and a positive attitude. He attacked and attacked and eventually caught Yusifov with a ko-uchi-gari for a waza-ari. This seemed to light a fire under the Azerbaijani fighter and he found a new gear.
Davlatov, not feeling that there had been a change in his opponent, continued to come forward and attempted to pick Yusifov up but he was ready and countered beautifully, scoring his own waza-ari. His transition was also on point and not settling for just an equaliser, Ahmad Yusifov circled and held his opponent for a second waza-ari.
Azerbaijan has their first world champion of these championships, a new hero who won gold as well as the hearts of his nation. After the final he said, “I always tried to keep positive thoughts in my mind and to believe that I could win, especially in front of this crowd. Their support was incredible. Every single person in the arena gave me energy and helped me throughout the competition. I felt that support very strongly and it pushed me to give everything I had. Now I am world champion and I feel great. This title belongs, in part, to everyone who supported me here today.”
What a contest! This 4 minutes had absolutely everything: speed, strength, skill, drama, intensity, acrobatics, courage. There was nothing missing.
As one attacked, the other made split-second decisions to defend or counter. Impressive awareness accompanied every choice and the accumulation of movements created a magnetic contest; it was impossible to turn away. A counter from Nagayama put a yuko on the board after 2 and a half minutes but there was still no indication of who would earn the nod at full time.
Nagayama held his ground, despite looking as though he may have picked up an injury during the later stages of the fight. Bliev could not repeat his bronze medal winning performance of 2025. Nagayama also missed out on a repeat performance but the bronze medal in Baku will certainly be some consolation; two world championship medals in as many years is no easy ask.
Giorgi Sardashvilli had tasted gold in the past and wanted to recreate the feeling of stepping on to the world championship podium. A positive, attacking style led him to do just that in Baku!
He out-attacked Yung Wei Yang, putting him under a great deal of pressure from the outset. As Yang began to collect penalties, Sardalashvili only grew more determined. Yang attempted to adjust but the Georgian had his strategy and a perfect rhythm.
A small chop-down from Sardalashvili created the conditions for some momentum to take hold and he spun Yang on to his back from a position already considered to be ne-waza. There he held him down for ippon. This young Georgian astounded everyone when he won his world title two years ago, but now he is proving that it wasn’t luck but the beginning of an impressive career.

articles.title_orig: Polish activists launch abortion pill locker to bypass near-total ban
articles.title_zh: Polish activists launch abortion pill locker to bypass near-total ban
articles.content_orig:
‘AbortOmat’ in Warsaw offers novel way to challenge country’s restrictions and allow women swift, anonymous access
They call it the “world’s first parcel locker for abortion pills”. Polish campaigners have launched a new means of distribution as part of their ongoing effort to skirt the country’s near-total ban on abortion.
Painted pink and framed by zebra-striped curtains, the 22-compartment “AbortOmat” in Warsaw allows women to access the pills swiftly and anonymously using a six-digit code. The service was envisaged for those who cannot or do not want to wait days for mail delivery due to a missed miscarriage or health complications, or who worry about receiving the pills at home.
“And why not?” said Kinga Jelinska, the director of the Women Help Women foundation and co-founder of the Abortion Dream Team, the two groups behind last week’s launch.
“You can order underwear, cosmetics, mascara, whatever and receive it practically the same or next day,” she said. “Why not abortion pills, where in some cases there might be more urgency?”
The innovation comes six years after people across Poland took to the streets to protest against the tightening of abortion laws that already ranked among the strictest in Europe, setting off the country’s largest demonstrations since the fall of communism. In 2023, the protests were credited with helping to propel Donald Tusk, and his promises to overhaul the laws within 100 days, into power.
Since then, political stagnation has set in, said Jelinska, citing comments made last year by Tusk in which the prime minister said there was “simply no majority” to change the laws to allow abortions until the 12th week of pregnancy. Tusk instead hinted that his government was intent on doing things differently, telling reporters that it would not prosecute those who helped to facilitate abortions.
While the possession or ingestion of abortion pills is not outlawed in Poland, provision of the medication or helping someone to obtain it is considered a crime punishable by up to three years in prison.
The locker offers a novel way to challenge these restrictions, said Jelinska. “It’s a little bit of a hack on the law,” she said. “The law is about directly giving to someone. So here we have a machine in between, which makes the legality of everything much more vague.”
The locker sits inside the abortion centre that was opened in March 2025 by the Abortion Dream Team. Described as the first of its kind in democratic Poland, it offers a safe space for people to consult on abortion options or receive support while they take the pill.
after newsletter promotion
Symbolically located across the street from the Polish parliament, the centre has allowed campaigners to shine a spotlight on the continued need for abortion access in Poland while also providing services to a wide array of people, said Jelinska. “It has exceeded our expectations.”
But it had also laid bare how few in power were willing to stand up for them, she said. “The one thing that has surprised us, and it speaks to the political situation, is that there are protests in front of the centre; three, sometimes four times a week.”
While usually less than a dozen people turn up, the protesters regularly use sirens and vuvuzelas to make their point, leaving campaigners worried that the noise levels would eventually result in neighbours asking the centre to relocate. “Neither the city or the police have reacted. So that has been a big disappointment to us,” said Jelinska.
It was a glimpse of how these organisations had increasingly felt abandoned by politicians, even as about 50,000 people in Poland contacted the wider network of pro-choice organisations last year seeking help, said Jelinska. “I think in Poland, abortion access won’t be solved by politics but by women and communities,” she said. “We cannot trust politicians with our own bodies.”

articles.title_orig: Houthis Claim Attack on Aramco as Yemen Conflict Escalates
articles.title_zh: Houthis Claim Attack on Aramco as Yemen Conflict Escalates
articles.content_orig:
The Saudi-led “Coalition to Support Legitimacy in Yemen” pledged full support on Sunday as Yemen’s internationally recognized government announced the start of a major military offensive aimed at rolling back recent gains by the Iran-backed Houthi movement.
Last month, the Iran-backed Houthis carried out a lightning offensive down the Red Sea coast, successfully seizing control of a key port and further putting pressure on the safety of international shipping.
Rashad al-Alimi, head of Yemen’s presidential council, said in a televised speech on Sunday that the ‌military ⁠operations aimed to reclaim the ​remaining ​territory held ‌by Houthis ⁠and restore ​state ​authority across the ⁠country.
An offensive had been widely expected amid dozens of Saudi airstrikes against Houthi positions and further Houthi gains in southern Yemen.
The renewed fighting has already forced tens of thousands of people from their homes, and what happens next could shift the balance of power in Yemen and further exacerbate an already bleak humanitarian crisis. Three out of every four families in parts of Yemen are going hungry because of the surge in fighting, the World Food Program said last week.
Al-Alimi said the decision to launch operations followed “the Houthi militias’ continued mobilization, escalation and attacks, as well as their threats against civilians, facilities, neighboring countries, and international shipping lanes.”
In a separate statement, military spokesperson Majid Al-Nuzaili said government forces had begun a “battle for liberation” aimed at ending Houthi control over remaining territory and restoring state institutions.
Al-Nuzaili also called on fighters aligned with the Houthis to lay down their arms and return to their homes, saying the government remained committed to protecting civilians during the offensive.
The Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said they will continue providing “full operational support” to Yemeni government forces in what he described as efforts to restore state institutions and end “the Houthi coup.”
Al-Maliki also accused the Houthis of continuing attacks against Saudi Arabia and international shipping in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandeb Strait.
“Such threats undermine regional and international security, jeopardize freedom of navigation and international trade, the lifeblood of the global economy,” he added.
Yemen’s Houthi-controlled armed forces said on Sunday that Saudi Arabia had carried out 106 air and missile strikes over the previous 24 hours targeting the capital Sanaa and other areas of the country.
The Houthi statement did not provide details on casualties or damage resulting from the reported attacks.
In retaliation for airstrikes against Sanaa and other locations, the Houthis claimed Sunday that they had struck vital Saudi energy facilities.
“The first targeted Aramco company in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, and the second targeted Aramco company in the Khurais area,” causing large fires at the targeted sites, a Houthi military statement said.
There has been no word from the Saudis on the claimed strikes.
Early in September, the Houthis took a swath of Yemen’s Red Sea coast as far south as the critical Bab al Mandeb waterway, a chokepoint for commercial shipping crossing into the Indian Ocean.
They announced that Saudi shipping trying to use the strait would be targeted, threatening additional pressure on global trade and energy routes.
The Houthis have fired ballistic missiles and drones at multiple targets in Saudi Arabia since late July, including industrial and energy infrastructure.
Much of the recent fighting has been in the southern region of Taiz, as the Houthis have sought to cut off government forces in the regional capital. The Houthis claimed on Sunday to have taken a critical highway linking Taiz with the seat of the Yemeni government in Aden.
Taiz is the third largest city in Yemen, with a population of several hundred thousands. It is also home to thousands of government troops.
Further east, in the al-Jawf region, the Houthis on Sunday claimed to have inflicted heavy casualties on government forces with a barrage of missiles and drones as they redeployed for the new offensive.
Yemeni government forces, backed by Saudi airstrikes and a blockade of Houthi areas, started fighting the Houthis more than a decade ago.
On Monday, officials from Saudi Arabia will convene with Turkish and Pakistani officials in Riyadh to discuss regional developments.
The meeting is part of the Strategic and Political Defense Committee, a NATO-style defense pact established in August , which is committed to organizing security and military cooperation in the region. The Saudi foreign ministry has said that it “does not represent an effort to establish a military axis or a sectarian bloc.”
The war in Yemen, which began in March 2015, had killed 377,000 people by the end of 2021, including those killed by direct and indirect causes, according to the United Nations. Over 150,000 of these deaths were the direct result of the armed conflict, it said, while more have died as a result of hunger and disease due to the humanitarian crisis caused by the war.
A 2022 UN-brokered truce brought a period of relatively low levels of hostilities between the two sides until violence surged again in August.

articles.title_orig: Evans ends Britain’s wait for world rally title after Solberg crashes two corners from glory
articles.title_zh: Evans ends Britain’s wait for world rally title after Solberg crashes two corners from glory
articles.content_orig:
Elfyn Evans becomes first British winner since 2001
Oliver Solberg’s hopes shattered by tumble down bank
⁠Elfyn Evans ended years of heartache, and a quarter-of-a-century wait for Britain, by winning the World Rally Championship title with Toyota after a dramatic season ⁠finale in Sardinia on Sunday.
The ⁠Welshman had been ​championship runner-up five times in the last six years but emerged triumphant after a final Powerstage duel with teammate Oliver Solberg ended with the charging Swede crashing ⁠out two corners from the finish while on course to take the crown.
Solberg, 25, ran wide and careered down a bank before getting the car back on the road. ⁠He still won the rally but lost the crucial bonus points on offer for the top five in the ​final stage.
Evans, with co-driver Scott Martin at his side, ‌became the first British world ‌rally champion since Englishman Richard Burns in 2001 and only the third since Scottish driver Colin McRae became ‌the first in 1995.
Sweden’s Solberg, son of Norway’s 2003 champion Petter, ended the season as runner-up. The final standings left Evans on 243 points, Solberg on 238 and Sami Pajari on 237 in what was also the end of an era for the sport with new regulations in force next year.
Evans said: “It hasn’t sunk in. I was sure it was over. I didn’t drive the best ‌stage but threw everything at it but it wasn’t clean. I feel for Oliver. He had an incredible weekend.” The Welshman completed his final run first and had to ​watch and wait to see whether he had done enough to take the title.
“I don’t really know what my reaction is, it’s surreal with how it happened. It’s a relief. It wouldn’t be my proudest way of winning it, but it’s job done,” added the 37-year-old, who finished fifth in the gravel rally.
Evans had started the rally – the ⁠final round after Saudi Arabia’s finale was cancelled due to conflict in the region – ​17 points clear of Finland’s Pajari, ​also in a Toyota, and 21 clear ​of Solberg.
after newsletter promotion
The Swede took control of the rally on Saturday, knowing he had nothing ​to lose and all to ‌gain, and started ​the final day 33.6 seconds ​clear of the field and the momentum swinging his way.
That feeling was reinforced when Evans lost time changing a wheel on Sunday’s penultimate stage, leaving the championship outcome hanging on the short final stage and the title going to which of the pair finished ahead of the other.
Toyota had already won the manufacturers’ championship.

articles.title_orig: Gavin Newsom on His Life in the Wine World
articles.title_zh: Gavin Newsom on His Life in the Wine World
articles.content_orig:
This story is from an installment of The Oeno Files , our weekly insider newsletter to the world of fine wine. Sign up here.
Long before setting his sights on Sacramento, Governor Gavin Newsom had one aspiration: to make fine wine more accessible. A lifelong wine lover who first connected with the fruit of the vine through his father, the San Francisco native cofounded PlumpJack wine shop there in 1992 with a group of partners that included family friend, oil heir, and composer Gordon Getty. Named for a Shakespeare character, the PlumpJack Group has since grown to include PlumpJack, Cade, and Odette wineries in Napa, and its leadership team includes general manager John Conover and Newsom’s sister, Hilary.
Elected mayor of San Francisco in 2003, Newsom’s interest in politics was piqued when the city’s department of health required him to install a mop sink in his carpeted wine shop. He began his career in government with a role in the San Francisco Parking and Traffic Commission before earning a spot on the city’s Board of Supervisors and then moved through the ranks of political office. Newsom placed his ownership interest in PlumpJack Group’s wineries, hotels, and restaurants into a blind trust when he was elected governor in 2018. Throughout his entire career, he continues to enjoy fine wine, especially bottles from Napa, Burgundy, Chablis, and Italy.
How did you first become interested in wine? Wine was one of the things I could connect with my dad about. Food, wine, and travel were a big part of his life. Because he could sometimes be emotionally hard to reach, wine became a kind of shared language between us—a way to sit together, talk, learn, and connect without having to force the conversation.
What was your journey toward opening the PlumpJack wine shop in 1992? It really started over dinner at the Balboa Cafe with my father and Pat Kelley, who had previously owned a wine store nearby. I became fixated on this idea of making fine wine more accessible—a store that wasn’t the discount rack but also wasn’t some precious place for the initiated, where people could discover great wine at an accessible price. I was 24, raised $174,000 from 15 friends and family, quit my job, and spent nearly two years fighting through permits and scraping the business together.
What is the origin of the name PlumpJack? PlumpJack is Sir John Falstaff, Shakespeare’s irreverent, larger-than-life character, and the inspiration for Gordon Getty’s opera. I loved that Falstaff mocked stuffiness and celebrated the absurdity of life. That was precisely the attitude we wanted to bring to wine.
How did you go from having a wine shop to opening wineries? The store worked, and two years later we opened PlumpJack Cafe with the same philosophy: exceptional wines without the extraordinary restaurant markup, including great Cabernets, Pinots, and Zinfandels by the glass. I’d always had an affinity for Oakville and Napa Cabernet, so when the opportunity came in 1995 to acquire a winery there, we jumped at it and eventually expanded to four wineries.
What are some of your favorite wines? I’ve always loved Oakville Cabernet. Groth and Silver Oak were two early favorites, but my tastes have always ranged beyond Napa, including Burgundy, Chablis, Pinot Noir, and Italian whites.
Do you consider yourself a wine drinker or collector? I’ve always been more interested in drinking and sharing wine than displaying it.
Under your leadership, in what ways has the state of California addressed the glut of wine grapes in the state that caused growers to rip out a reported 40,000 acres of vines in the past year and allow 100,000 tons of grapes to remain unharvested? Government cannot manufacture consumer demand or wave a wand and correct an oversupply that developed over many years. Across the agriculture industry, we’ve supported California growers through research, pest prevention, water resilience, and market development, but I’ve also gone out of my way throughout my public career to ensure my personal history in the wine business never influences state policy. And right now, one of the worst things Washington could do is make a difficult market even harder. President Trump’s trade war with Canada has helped trigger retaliation and restrictions on American wine in what has been our largest export market. It’s exactly the opposite of what California growers need.
There is a perception that vineyards and wineries are owned by rich people who don’t need help from the government to survive. How much truth is there to that perception? The industry is incredibly diverse. Yes, there are wealthy vineyard owners, but there are also thousands of farmers, small and multigenerational wineries, farmworkers, cellar workers, truck drivers, restaurant and hotel employees whose livelihoods depend on this industry. California wine alone supports more than 422,000 jobs in our state. That’s why Trump’s tariffs are so harmful.
Why did you title your book Young Man In A Hurry ? It actually came from a 2009 Economist article about me—not exactly a compliment at the time—and years later I realized how much truth there was in it. I came to see it less as somebody else’s critique than as a self-critique: the impatience, ambition, insecurity, and constant need to keep moving that have shaped so much of my life.
If readers of your book come away with one impression, what do you hope it to be? That people are more complicated than their caricatures, including me. Writing this book forced me to scrutinize rather than sanitize my life, to understand my parents and my family differently, and ultimately to discover things about myself that I hadn’t fully understood before.
Completely theoretical, of course … but what wines would you like to see served at a White House dinner? For now, my answer is anything but Trump Wine.

articles.title_orig: EURETINA 2026: Real-world evidence on retinal biosimilars
articles.title_zh: EURETINA 2026: Real-world evidence on retinal biosimilars
articles.content_orig:
Ashish Sharma, MD, on what real-world data show about switching and long-term outcomes with retinal biosimilars.
As real-world data on retinal biosimilars accumulates, the conversation among clinicians has shifted from whether these agents are comparable to the reference product to how they actually perform in everyday practice. Ashish Sharma, MD, founder and chair of the International Retina Biosimilar Study Group (Inter-BIOS), presented real-world evidence on aflibercept-ayyyh and FYB-201 (Ravegza) at EURETINA 2026 , held 1-4 October in Vienna, Austria.
In this Q&A conversation with Ophthalmology Times Europe , Sharma—who is also consultant retina and director of clinical research at Lotus Eye Hospital and Institute in Coimbatore, India—discusses what the APEX and APEX-LT datasets show about long-term outcomes, what the evidence says about switching from reference products, and what still needs to happen before biosimilar access translates into broader patient access to anti-VEGF therapy.
Note: Transcript edited lightly for clarity and length.
Ashish Sharma, MD: The biggest shift has been from asking whether biosimilars are scientifically comparable to asking how they perform in everyday clinical practice.
When retinal biosimilars first entered the market, there was understandably a degree of caution around extrapolation, switching and the possibility of unexpected safety signals with repeated intravitreal administration.
Today, we have moved considerably beyond that initial uncertainty. We now have increasing real-world experience across different retinal diseases, geographies and treatment settings. At Inter-BIOS, our objective has been to complement regulatory evidence with large, multicentre real-world datasets that clinicians can relate directly to their own practice.
I think the conversation is therefore becoming much more practical: Which patients are appropriate, how should we switch, what happens to treatment intervals, and can biosimilars help improve access without compromising outcomes?
Sharma: The APEX program is particularly valuable because it looks at aflibercept-ayyyh in the environment in which we actually treat patients.
Our early APEX study included 707 treatment-naïve eyes receiving 1,912 injections and demonstrated significant functional and anatomical improvements across retinal vascular diseases, with a favorable short-term safety profile.
The larger APEX safety dataset extends that experience to more than 52,000 intravitreal injections, allowing us to look much more closely at uncommon ocular safety events. The published APEX safety study found no new safety signal, which is important when clinicians are evaluating a new intravitreal biosimilar.
The APEX-LT work is another important step because clinicians need to know not only whether a biosimilar works initially, but whether visual, anatomical and safety outcomes remain consistent over longer-term real-world treatment.
I would emphasize that these are observational real-world studies and should be interpreted alongside the randomized comparative evidence. Taken together, however, the accumulating evidence is reassuring and consistent with the established biosimilarity of aflibercept-ayyyh.
Sharma: Switching has probably been one of the biggest practical questions from retina specialists.
The important message from the evidence available so far is that a transition from the reference product to aflibercept-ayyyh has not identified a new efficacy or safety concern. The randomized comparative study included a transition from reference aflibercept to aflibercept-ayyyh and found no clinically meaningful differences after the switch.
Real-world data are now adding an important layer to this. In a separate 1,000-eye real-world analysis, 91% of eyes had switched from prior anti-VEGF therapy, with visual acuity remaining stable among switchers over the observed follow-up period.
What we still need is longer-term, larger and more diverse datasets to understand treatment intervals, durability and switching patterns in different healthcare environments. That is precisely where collaborative real-world evidence such as Inter-BIOS can make an important contribution.
Sharma: I would be cautious about making a direct head-to-head comparison because these are different molecules and different real-world datasets, rather than a randomized comparison between the two biosimilars.
Our FORCE experience with FYB-201 has been very encouraging. The original FORCE study provided multicentre real-world evidence across retinal vascular diseases, and our recent Middle Eastern extension provided additional experience with Ravegza in Saudi Arabia and Uptera in Jordan.
What I find particularly valuable is that we are seeing real-world experience accumulate across different biosimilars, different regions and different clinical settings.
For retina specialists, the broader message is that biosimilar adoption should be guided by the totality of evidence for each individual product, rather than assuming that all biosimilars are identical simply because they belong to the same category.
Sharma: I believe biosimilars have the potential to improve access, but we should be careful not to assume that approval automatically translates into access.
Cost is certainly an important component, but access is influenced by many factors—reimbursement policies, physician confidence, hospital formularies, procurement systems, patient awareness and local healthcare economics.
What we are seeing globally is a very diverse picture. In some markets, biosimilars are already becoming an important part of retinal practice; in others, adoption remains slower.
This is why I think real-world evidence is so important. If we can demonstrate consistent clinical outcomes, safety, switching experience and durability, while creating a more economically sustainable treatment environment, then biosimilars can become an important tool for expanding access to anti-VEGF therapy.
Ultimately, the goal is not simply to increase biosimilar utilization. The goal is to enable more patients who need anti-VEGF therapy to actually receive and continue appropriate treatment.

articles.title_orig: Two dead, 35 wounded in shooting at Georgia block party
articles.title_zh: Two dead, 35 wounded in shooting at Georgia block party
articles.content_orig:
Two people were killed and 35 others were wounded in a shooting at a block party early Sunday in south-central Georgia.
The Georgia Bureau of Investigation said in a press release that shots were fired at about 1:25 a.m. in Vienna, a rural community about two hours south of Atlanta. Local station WALB News 10 described the event as a homecoming party.
Dooly County Sheriff’s Office deputies were patrolling the party at the time, the bureau said. Two people were pronounced dead at the scene, and the wounded were taken to several regional hospitals.
The bureau declined to say whether authorities had determined a motive or identified a suspect.
“The investigation remains active and ongoing. At this time, no additional information is available for release,” Lydia Bullard, the bureau’s public affairs specialist, said in a statement to NBC News.
Brett Watts, the Dooly County coroner, said the two people who died were both males, ages 20 and 23. Each had single gunshot wounds, Watts said, though an autopsy by the medical examiner’s office, scheduled for Friday, could provide a fuller picture. He said the men’s families have been notified.
Aria Bendix is the breaking health reporter for NBC News Digital.
