articles.title_orig: Microsoft adds alternate way to download and install Windows 11 26H2 easily
articles.title_zh: Microsoft adds alternate way to download and install Windows 11 26H2 easily
articles.content_orig:
Windows powers how people around the world work, learn, create, and connect every day. Today, we’re announcing the availability of the Windows 11 2026 Update, also known as Windows 11, version 26H2. Built on the same servicing foundation as recent Windows 11 releases, version 26H2 delivers the latest Windows innovations with a streamlined update experience designed to minimize disruption and help you stay secure, productive, and up to date.
As organizations and individuals continue to expect faster deployments and less downtime, Windows 11, version 26H2 takes advantage of the same modern servicing technologies that have simplified recent feature updates. For many eligible devices, moving to version 26H2 is as simple as installing a small enablement package, allowing people to start using this new release with minimal download size, quick installation, and a single restart.
Windows 11, version 26H2 is delivered as an enablement package for eligible devices running Windows 11, versions 25H2 and 24H2.
An enablement package is a lightweight update that activates new features already included in the operating system through previous monthly servicing updates. Because versions 26H2, 25H2, and 24H2 share a common servicing branch and underlying codebase, many of the components required for version 26H2 are already present on devices before the feature update becomes available.
This approach enables a significantly faster update experience compared to a traditional operating system upgrade. For eligible devices, installation is similar to a monthly update, requiring only a small download and a quick restart to transition to Windows 11, version 26H2.
As with every Windows release, version 26H2 includes the latest quality, reliability, and security improvements designed to help protect people and organizations while delivering a dependable Windows experience.
Windows 11, version 26H2 is now available for eligible devices running Windows 11, versions 25H2 and 24H2.
To be among the first to receive the update, go to Settings > Windows Update and turn on Get the latest updates as soon as they’re available . Once your device is eligible, you’ll see the option to download and install Windows 11, version 26H2.
As always, we take a measured and data-driven approach to broad availability and will be releasing version 26H2 using a controlled feature rollout. During rollout, we might place safeguard holds on devices where we detect a known compatibility issue that could impact the update experience. We will continue expanding availability over time and provide updates through the Windows release health hub.
Windows 11, version 26H2 is available now through the tools organizations use to manage Windows updates, including Windows Autopatch and the Microsoft 365 admin center [i] .
Existing management tools, update rings, policies, and deployment practices can continue to be used. We recommend that commercial and education customers begin targeted deployments to validate applications, devices, and business-critical workflows before expanding deployment more broadly throughout their organizations.
Windows 11, version 26H2 continues the annual Windows feature update cadence, with a new Windows 11 feature update released during the second half of the calendar year. As with previous annual releases, installing version 26H2 resets the support lifecycle for supported editions of Windows 11. That means 24 months of support for Home and Pro editions and 36 months of support for Enterprise and Education editions.
Select features and enhancements initially released as disabled by default in version 25H2 will be enabled by default in version 26H2. You can find more information on these features, plus guidance to help with planning and deployment, in the Windows IT Pro Blog .
We recommend updating eligible devices to Windows 11, version 26H2 to take advantage of the latest Windows innovations, quality improvements, and security enhancements.
We’ll continue to closely monitor the rollout and share information about known issues, safeguards, and rollout progress through the Windows release health hub and official Windows communications channels.
Thank you for your feedback and partnership as we continue to improve Windows for people and organizations around the world. We love to hear about your experience, so please keep your comments and suggestions coming in via Feedback Hub.
[i] Downloads in the Microsoft 365 admin center and similar channels may be delayed.

articles.title_orig: Houthis say Saudi Arabia launched dozens of strikes on Yemen capital
articles.title_zh: Houthis say Saudi Arabia launched dozens of strikes on Yemen capital
articles.content_orig:
The Yemeni army says it has carried out hundreds of strikes on the capital, Sanaa, and other areas held by the Iran-backed Houthis, as the battle for control of the country’s most populated regions intensifies.
Colonel Majed Abdullah al-Nazili, the spokesman for Yemen’s internationally recognised government forces, said on Saturday that the military “executed 257 precision targeting operations” against Houthi sites, movements, and military capabilities.
The army used “warplanes, drones, artillery, missiles, and rocket launchers”, he added in a post on X.
Al-Nazili said initial estimates indicate the operations killed at least 700 Houthi rebels and destroyed “strategic and high-value military targets”, including 170 combat vehicles and heavy equipment.
The army spokesman did not mention any casualties among government forces.
The strikes “had a direct impact on the [Houthi] militia’s combat capability and limited its ability to continue its attacks against civilians in their homes and villages”, he said.
Saturday’s operations targeted Sanaa, Midi, Baqim, and the front lines in al-Jawf, Marib, al-Bayda, and Lahij, with the heaviest operational efforts concentrated around Taiz, al-Nazili added.
On Friday, al-Nazili said Yemen’s government forces had carried out nearly 500 military operations, killing or wounding 1,540 Houthi rebels in 24 hours.
The government-held city of Taiz has become a focal point of the renewed fighting .
Al Jazeera’s Maha Ali, reporting from Taiz on Saturday, said the region is seeing continued escalation and intense fighting across several fronts around the city, with some of the fiercest fighting happening on its western outskirts.
The Houthis have used an exceptionally heavy volume of fire during the assault, she noted, adding that the sound of continuing artillery fire, particularly from the Houthi side targeting western areas, could still be heard.
Residents are appealing for evacuation as the shelling continues, Ali reported, adding that there have been civilian casualties in the fighting, including from a shell that hit a residential area in Dhubab, killing a baby who died from shrapnel injuries.
On the Samaa front, she said, the Houthis made advances on Friday in the mountainous area, and fierce clashes are continuing there between government forces and the rebels. Several field sources told Ali that large numbers of residents have left Samaa, something, she said, that had not happened on this scale in more than a decade.
Following those clashes, Yemeni government forces took control of the Samaa fort, southeast of the city of Taiz, after heavy fighting, the government-run Saba news agency reported.
A military source told Saba that the armed forces, backed by local popular resistance fighters from the Samaa district, secured the fort after “violent battles”, leaving dozens of Houthi fighters killed or wounded while others fled.
On Saturday, the army’s media official Ammar al-Sami’i told Al Jazeera that the government had closed the al-Houban crossing in Taiz.
The crossing had previously been closed for nine years and was later reopened to civilians in 2024 for “humanitarian reasons”, Sami’i said, as the road is one of Yemen’s most important connections between territory held by the opposing sides. It connects Houthi-held al-Houban to government-held Taiz city.
Sami’i said security reasons are behind the closure, following an attempt by the Houthis to infiltrate Taiz via the road, attacks in the vicinity and a general military build-up.
A fragile truce struck between the government and the Houthis in 2022 collapsed in July this year, and fighting in Yemen has escalated significantly since then.
In mid-September, the Houthis swept across parts of western Yemen, seizing the port city of Mocha and key strategic islands in the Bab al-Mandeb strait.
Since then, anti-Houthi forces have largely stabilised the front lines.
Hundreds of thousands of people have been displaced since the fighting restarted.
Yemen has been embroiled in civil war since the Houthis seized the capital of Sanaa in 2014, forcing the internationally recognised government to retreat to Aden.

articles.title_orig: Departure comes as the state investigates what went wrong during Pike's lethal injection.
articles.title_zh: Departure comes as the state investigates what went wrong during Pike's lethal injection.
articles.content_orig:
Gov. Lee has appointed a former U.S. attorney to investigate the failed attempt.
Tennessee Department of Correction Commissioner Frank Strada said he will resign days after Christa Pike was hospitalized in the wake of a botched execution attempt, according to Gov. Bill Lee.
The Tennessee governor's statement on Saturday did not directly reference the situation with Pike, who is currently "critically ill," unconscious and on a ventilator in a hospital following the Sept. 30 failed execution. In the announcement, Strada said that stepping aside was "in the best interest of Tennesseans as the independent review moves forward."
"I believe this review is entirely appropriate and necessary, and I look forward to doing everything I can to help determine exactly what occurred," he said in a statement.
Lee said he accepted Strada's resignation and the commissioner would leave his post at the end of the month.
"Commissioner Strada has served with integrity, and I appreciate his willingness to put the interests of Tennesseans first during this difficult moment," the governor said in a statement.
An interim commissioner will be announced at a later date, the statement noted.
On Sunday, the governor's office announced that former U.S. Attorney Ed Stanton had been appointed "to conduct an independent review of the Tennessee Department of Correction’s actions in carrying out the court-ordered sentence of Christa Gail Pike."
The review "will seek to determine whether the protocol was followed and consider whether additional recommendations are necessary to ensure the State’s protocol continues to be lawful and effective," according to the statement.
"The State previously retained Stanton in 2022 to conduct an independent review of Tennessee's lethal injection protocol. His work prompted the State and Attorney General’s Office to substantially rewrite the protocol before executions resumed," the statement further said.
Pike's attorneys, Randy Spivey, Kelly Gleason, Stephen Ferrell and Luke Ihnen, responded to the Strada stepping down in their own statement.
"The resignation of Commissioner Strada is justified, but it does nothing to help Christa now. What happened to her Wednesday reflects a systemic failure that goes far beyond any one person," they wrote. "We hope the Governor's call for a full, independent review will expose the profound problems within Tennessee's entire death penalty system."
Strada's resignation comes after questions arose about his record as a correction official and other botched executions.
Strada began serving as the Deputy Director for the Arizona Department of Correction in January 2020 after serving as the director of operations for private prison operator The Geo Group, according to his LinkedIn page.
During his tenure in Arizona, he oversaw prisons where advocates say three executions were botched.
According to the Death Penalty Information Center, each of the three executions Arizona conducted in 2022 was "visibly problematic."
Those three executions were the state's first since 2014, when the lethal injection of Joseph Wood took nearly two hours and resulted in him visibly struggling to breathe.
After the three executions in 2022 went wrong, Arizona Gov. Katie Hobbs signed an executive order directing an independent review of the state's execution policy and paused lethal injections in the state.
About a month before Hobbs signed her executive order, Tennessee's Gov. Lee announced that Strada would take over the state's Department of Correction.
At the time of his appointment, Tennessee too had paused executions after a 2022 incident when a lethal injection was halted at the last minute because officials failed to properly test the drugs.
By December 2024 -- under Strada's leadership -- the Tennessee Department of Correction issued new protocols to resume lethal injections in the state.
Pike's attorneys said Friday that she is in the hospital on a ventilator and being "treated for the serious effects of the pentobarbital administered during the execution attempt, including significant injuries to both arms ."
The attorneys filed an emergency motion Friday in Davidson County Chancery Court seeking an order requiring the Tennessee Department of Correction to preserve all relevant evidence related to the execution attempt.
According to the motion, Pike "could be heard crying, whimpering, and breathing loudly" while being administered two lethal doses of pentobarbital, at one point stating that her arm "feels like it's about to burst open." At least seven needles were used to gain IV access, with one "bent in a 90-degree angle when it was removed," it stated.
The motion described pentobarbital, a sedating medication, as being "caustic and highly alkaline" and that it "burns upon contact." Both of Pike's arms were "swollen, burned, and blistered" when she arrived at a Nashville-area hospital, the motion stated.
"Hospital staff are working to save Ms. Pike's life and to clear the pentobarbital from her system," the motion stated.
Pike, the first woman the state planned to execute in over 200 years, had raised concerns about a lethal injection in the months prior to her scheduled execution, arguing that her "thrombocytosis, post traumatic stress disorder and small veins 'make it sure or very likely that there is a substantial risk that she will experience unnecessary and superadded pain and suffering, terror, and disgrace,'" the motion stated.
Pike is the first person reported to have survived lethal injection after being given medications, according to the Death Penalty Information Center, whose executive director referred to the failed attempt as "the worst we've ever seen and unlike any other botched execution in the modern era."
The governor has ordered a "third-party review" and a temporary halt to scheduled executions after the execution attempt.
"So far as we know, the Department of Correction followed exactly the protocol as outlined," the governor told reporters on Thursday. He said the state needs to know "why the outcome is different this time than ever before."
ABC News' Peter Charalambous contributed to this report.

articles.title_orig: Russia pledges to continue massive strikes on Kyiv, urges foreign diplomats to leave city
articles.title_zh: Russia pledges to continue massive strikes on Kyiv, urges foreign diplomats to leave city
articles.content_orig:
At least five people have been killed in a series of long-range strikes carried out by Kyiv and Moscow.
Russia attacked a Liberian-flagged ship in Ukraine’s Odesa region, killing one person and injuring three, the Ukrainian Sea Ports Authority said on Saturday in a statement on Telegram. Another 12 crew members were safely evacuated from the ship. Three were injured.
Russia has in effect blockaded Ukraine’s Black Sea ports – formerly a key global source of food exports – by attacking civilian vessels carrying grain and steel, dealing a heavy blow to the Ukrainian economy.
Two people were reportedly killed in a Ukrainian strike on the Russia-occupied Luhansk region of Ukraine, according to the Moscow-installed governor.
In the occupied Zaporizhia region, Russian-installed authorities said one person was killed and 10 others injured in a Ukrainian drone attack.
Russian media also reported that one person was killed in a Ukrainian drone attack on Russia’s Belgorod region, which sits just across the border from Ukraine.
Elsewhere, a Russian attack on Kyiv’s Northern Bridge injured two people. It is the second bridge Russia has attacked in the Ukrainian capital in the space of two days.
Also on Saturday, Russia’s Foreign Ministry issued another warning to diplomats and foreigners in Ukraine’s capital, urging them to leave the city or risk being harmed.
Many foreign embassies are still operating in Kyiv.
Russia’s all-out war on Ukraine is in its fifth year and shows little sign of slowing down.
Russian battlefield gains have slowed to a near-record low, with Ukrainian counterattacks, including one ongoing push around the town of Lyman in the east, mitigating Russian territorial gains elsewhere.
Russia has increased its attacks on civilian infrastructure in recent months, including with the growing use of jet-powered long-range strike drones, which move faster and are harder to shoot down.
Ukraine has also engaged in significant long-range strikes, including targeting Russian oil infrastructure and military-industrial facilities deep inside Russian territory.

articles.title_orig: Woman told Cornell investigators she 'felt like bait' during alleged gang rape
articles.title_zh: Woman told Cornell investigators she 'felt like bait' during alleged gang rape
articles.content_orig:
As outrage builds around the case involving a Cornell University student allegedly gang-raped in a fraternity house in October 2024, the university’s president has broken his silence with a statement Saturday.
Jane Doe’s alleged experiences raise “heartbreaking and troubling issues about sexual assault, dehumanization, and aspects of party culture, alcohol, and drug use,” Kotlikoff said in his video statement .
The Cornell president added the allegations raise questions around the initial investigation, saying the university does not have “all the answers” but is committed to investigating and finding them. He said next week, Cornell’s board of trustees will announce an independent review into the handling of the 2024 case by an outside law firm.
While Cornell had released a statement after Doe filed her lawsuit in September and later launched an FAQ page on the allegations, Saturday’s remarks from Kotlikoff mark his first on-camera statement on the case.
Kotlikoff said he backs legislative efforts to change New York’s sexual assault law and Hochul’s decision to appoint a special prosecutor in the investigation – a move the university previously told CNN it supported.
While the criminal investigation and review are underway, the university will work to strengthen programs surrounding sexual assault prevention and education, mental health and substance use, he added.
Addressing frustrations surrounding Cornell’s communications about the case, he said “we will make a greater effort to explain what we can, to provide context about the actions Cornell has taken, and to be more transparent” within the confines of legal and policy limits.
Toward the end of his statement, Kotlikoff signaled support for reviewing the role of Greek organizations in campus life. “We will reengage students, alumni, and other members of our community to examine how we preserve what is valuable about Greek life while strengthening individual accountability, transparency, and a culture in which every member understands their responsibility to protect the safety and well-being of others,” he said.
Doe’s attorney, Thomas Giuffra, said he is hopeful but wary about the promises Kotlikoff made. “We are hopeful that his statement is backed up by meaningful reforms that leads to real change for the sake of the students at Cornell,” he told CNN in a statement Saturday.
Snapchat messages , a Cornell disciplinary panel’s decision, a cache of documents from the university’s formal Title IX investigation obtained by The New York Times and phone recordings by Jane Doe reviewed by ABC News have shed new light on what may have happened in the fraternity house. The sources also help clarify Doe’s reported frame of mind at points on the night that began October 19, 2024, and how her understanding of the events changed as she processed her trauma in the following weeks.
When Doe first went to campus police, authorities documented that she reported “she was recently raped by 8-10 men at the Chi Phi fraternity house,” according to documents reviewed by ABC News. CNN has asked campus police for a copy of the report.
The phrase does not appear in the six-page statement sent to prosecutors.
Cornell is facing scrutiny because the university initially said campus police investigated the allegations in 2024 and “shared all investigatory information with the Tompkins County District Attorney’s Office.” But the school later changed its statement , now saying police investigated the allegations in 2024 and “shared the victim’s sworn statement and the Snapchat screenshot” with the DA’s office.
Van Houten previously said his office did not bring criminal charges because of Doe’s six-page statement. He later said his office had access to some Snapchat messages exchanged during the alleged assault in a group chat titled, “Chi Phi Actives.” Images of one Snapchat chain obtained by CNN include a photo of Doe in a room at the fraternity house during the time she describes being assaulted.
‘I am Jane Doe’: Online campaign to protect Cornell plaintiff
Doe also made an explicit allegation of rape in her interview that was not included in the six-page statement furnished to prosecutors, according to WCBS. Although Doe did recount being hit and feeling emotionally coerced in the statement, it did not include some stronger language or allegations she used in her interview, according to The New York Times, citing documents it obtained.
Among the documents obtained by the Times also were records showing the district attorney’s office declined to review any additional evidence gathered by the campus police department beyond the six-page statement signed by Doe. A Cornell police investigator spoke to a member of the district attorney’s staff on November 25, 2024, about reviewing additional evidence, the Times said. By that time, university police had conducted more interviews and reviewed chat messages, the Times report said.
But prosecutors did not express interest in the additional evidence because they had decided that, based on Doe’s statement, “Criminal charges would not be pursued in this case,” a Cornell police investigator said in a note documenting the call. When reached for comment, the district attorney staff member referred all questions to the district attorney, the Times reported.
A ‘loophole’ in New York’s rape law may have shut the door on criminal charges in the Cornell case. It’s not the first time
Van Houten told the Times by email that any additional records gathered by the Cornell police were “not pertinent to our analysis because we had Jane Doe’s comprehensive account of the events.” CNN reached out to Van Houten’s office for comment Friday.
CNN obtained a copy of a heavily redacted, 99-page document summarizing key evidence included in a Cornell disciplinary panel’s decision, which supports the Times’ findings about how Doe later came to understand the night’s events as assault. The panel’s decision details more than 50 interviews, including with six of the seven accused men.
Additionally, Jane Doe three weeks after the incident asked the fraternity member who invited her to the house that night, “Do you remember how any of these guys walked in?” her phone recordings reviewed by ABC News indicate.
He made no mention of his group chat invitation, ABC News reported, instead explaining to Doe, “The door was just unlocked. … The party was sort of like crowded. … There was nowhere else to go.”
Doe told him, “If I wanted to take this somewhere, what y’all did would be classified as gang rape,” she told him, ABC News reported, noting Doe’s recorded phone calls to at least three of the fraternity brothers were later turned over to university investigators.
One of the men Doe has accused of sexual assault reportedly sent her this text message: “I just wanted to apologize for how things went down the other night,” according to records obtained by The New York Times and corroborated by Doe’s attorney. The sender said he and another male allegedly involved felt terrible and too under the influence of drugs and alcohol to “shut it down and kick people out before it got way out of hand.”
“I’m so sorry,” another alleged attacker told Doe around the same time in a message ABC News reviewed. “I feel so bad for you, dude.”
The initial university investigation led to suspensions and expulsions for the accused students, according to Doe’s attorney, the barring of the fraternity chapter from campus and the launch of a sexual assault task force. Four of the Chi Phi fraternity members acknowledged having sexual contact with Doe but said their interactions had been consensual. The others denied participating in sexual encounters, the Times reported.
Amid the renewed investigation, court documents show a Chi Phi fraternity member named as a defendant in Doe’s civil suit has been petitioning New York state courts to invalidate a university disciplinary decision that found him responsible for attempted sexual exploitation.

articles.title_orig: Canada scores a dairy win on U.S. soil as farmers grumble about Trump's trade war
articles.title_zh: Canada scores a dairy win on U.S. soil as farmers grumble about Trump's trade war
articles.content_orig:
On the most elite stage in the world of competitive dairy, a Canadian teenager and her "favourite cow" scored two major wins while on U.S. soil.
Never heard of competitive dairy? Let me assure you, it's a really big deal. One win — let alone two — at the World Dairy Expo in Madison, Wisc., can be life changing for farmers and their cows.
It can boost the value of an animal by tens of thousands of dollars. Future offspring can become more valuable too. And of course, there's an element of national pride, especially when Canada and the U.S. are locked in a trade war.
Alyson Doiron, a 16-year-old high school student from Cap-Sante, Que., glows as she poses for photos with her aforementioned favourite cow — Arolene Dempsey Ella, who goes by "Ella" for short, was the five-year-old cow awarded the top prize at the International Junior Holstein Show.
"She's an easy cow to work with. We love her so much," Doiron told CBC News.
Doiron cheered and cried as she was given the prestigious honour on Ella's behalf, at the Expo on Sunday. Even though this is a global gathering, the actual competitions are between animals from Canadian and American farms, due to health and safety regulations.
"This means a lot to me," she said with a nod to her home province. "It just proves that in Quebec, the [cow] show is really really strong," she said.
The win on Sunday was just the start of a very big week for Doiron and Ella.
In the arena where the cows are judged, Canadian, American and Mexican flags hang in the rafters. It is a reminder, as constant as the smell of manure, that cross-border competition and co-operation are valued in this space.
"I think it's important for us to be here," said Brian Carscadden, the executive senior manager and part owner of Blondin Sires, a Quebec-based dairy company that has milk production and artificial insemination operations.
"If you think of the Westminster Dog Show, it's not unlike that. If you can win that, you've got a dog that's worth some money. It's the same here with your cow."
Carscadden and his team drove more than 1,500 kilometres from St. Placide to Madison, with 25 cows in trailers in tow. He says his business has not been affected by the trade war yet, and that it does not come up often in conversations at the Expo.
"There's jokes here and there," from his American friends, he said, along with "the odd snide remark … that makes things interesting."
"I always advise my Canadian colleagues that it's not our country, it's not our politics, don't talk about it."
Americans at the Expo are far more direct.
The trade war is a sore point for some, including voters who are connecting dots between U.S. President Donald Trump's broad economic agenda and increases in the cost of living.
"There is no lowering of grocery prices, no lowering of gas prices. I mean obviously it's all going higher and it makes me struggle," said Paula Lawver.
She's a single mom from a farming community in Indiana, and is at the Expo with a group of students from her son's high school. She describes herself as a conservative voter with conservative values, but does not consider herself a Republican.
She calls the dispute with Canada "nonsense," and says it will influence her vote in the midterm elections this November. Lawver says she will not support candidates in favour of tariffs and trade wars.
Seth Muck, a farmer from New York state, says he too may reconsider how he votes in the midterms.
He says in the past he's voted "hard, hard Republican, hard conservative." But after feeling the impact of Trump's global trade agenda, he's considering backing candidates with a "bit more moderate-type agenda."
Muck says his cash crops and farm inputs have been affected the most, noting that the price of fertilizer is double what he paid last year. Though he still holds out hope that economic conditions could improve.
"Perhaps it's going to take a bit … like ripping off a Band-Aid," he said.
Even among those willing to be more patient with Trump and his economic vision, CBC News did not find any Americans at this Expo supportive of the heated rhetoric that has upended the Canada-U.S. relationship.
"I think it's needless, pointless and childish. Both sides," said Gary Craugh, a retired farmer from Wisconsin.
'You will pay': Trump adviser warns Canada not to 'interfere' with U.S. midterms
Another retired farmer from Wisconsin, John Galgowski, says he's baffled by it all.
"I throw up my hands and go, 'Why are we doing this?'"
Galgowski does not support the Trump administration, and says the way the country has been run since Trump returned to office has only reaffirmed his position.
"It's just bad times," he said.
The way these voters described their experience is very different from how the Trump administration is framing the moment.
Trump says 'very bad' Canada is being 'taught a little lesson' as trade action escalates
U.S. bans on imported Canadian motorcycle, dairy, alcohol products take effect as trade war drags on
About 120 kilometres from the Expo, in Milwaukee, U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer hosted a gathering of G20 trade ministers, where he unapologetically advocated for the "America first" trade agenda, arguing that the strategy is working.
"American workers and their families are better off now than they were before President Trump took office," Greer said as he read from prepared remarks.
Greer's defence of the Trump administration's policies suggests there are no plans to change course anytime soon.
Which means the trade war with Canada is poised to grind on.
Even if the country-to-country tensions won't go away, Canada did score one more win at the World Dairy Expo.
On Friday, Doiron proudly paraded Ella in front of the judges on the arena floor, competing for one of the week’s largest titles: Supreme Junior Show Champion.
It's a moment that almost didn’t happen. Doiron says she helped raise Ella, but when her parents unexpectedly sold the cow, she was devastated.
"I was so mad at my parents, because she was just the cow I liked," she said, recalling the way she loved all of Ella's spots as a kid.
Doiron was determined to be reunited with her favourite cow, and when the opportunity arose, she re-purchased Ella, despite objections from her parents. "I need to bring this cow home," she told her mom.
The reunion was clearly meant to be.
In front of a packed arena, Doiron and Ella’s big moment finally arrived — the cow was named Supreme Junior Show Champion, a victory for all of Canada.
Katie Simpson is a foreign correspondent with CBC News based in Washington. Prior to joining the team in D.C., she spent six years covering Parliament Hill in Ottawa and nearly a decade covering local and provincial issues in Toronto.

articles.title_orig: Two Iranians charged over alleged plot targeting Jewish community in UK
articles.title_zh: Two Iranians charged over alleged plot targeting Jewish community in UK
articles.content_orig:
Two Iranian nationals charged with planning an attack against the Jewish community in northern England have appeared in a London court.
The UK Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said on Friday that Rahman Salehi, 34, and Salam Ahmadyan, 36, were charged with “preparing to commit or assisting another to commit an act of terrorism” in Manchester “on or before” Yom Kippur, the Jewish Day of Atonement, which began at sundown on September 20.
After appearing in Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Saturday, the men who did not enter a plea were remanded into custody. Their next hearing is set at London’s Old Bailey court for October 23.
“It is alleged that the two men were in contact with an overseas third-party who may be in Iran in relation to the plot,” police said in a separate statement on Friday.
Details of the alleged plot have not been released, but police have confirmed its “disruption”.
Counterterrorism police said Salehi and Ahmadyan, both arrested in Manchester on September 20, allegedly tried to acquire components and equipment to make an improvised explosive device and conducted reconnaissance on potential targets for attack.
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said Salehi and Ahmadyan arrived in the UK on a small boat from Europe several years ago. One of the men had been granted asylum and the other had a live asylum claim, the Home Office said.
“It is no secret that this country faces a range of serious threats from the Iranian regime,” she said in a statement.
“They target our Jewish communities and try to silence their critics overseas, often through proxies and criminal networks to hide their involvement,” she added.
Iran has denied similar accusations.
The charges come a year after two people were killed in a knife and gun attack by a British citizen of Syrian descent at the Heaton Park Hebrew Congregation Synagogue in northern Manchester on October 2, 2025.
“I’m aware that the news of this alleged plot coming during the High Holy day period has caused a great deal of concern to the Jewish community, as well as with the wider public,” Deputy Assistant Commissioner Vicki Evans, senior national coordinator for counterterrorism policing, said on Friday.
“It also coincides with the anniversary of the devastating terrorist attack last year at Heaton Park synagogue and comes in a wider context of increasing antisemitic incidents across the UK.”
Detectives said there was no connection between Friday’s charges and the suspected plot involving the RAF Fairford air base, over which a dual UK-Iranian national was arrested on Thursday, according to the Reuters news agency.
Britain said Tehran had been involved in an alleged plot earlier this week targeting an airbase used by the US to launch attacks against Iran.
Iran denied any involvement in the RAF Fairford plot and said speculation would “fuel Iranophobia propaganda”.

articles.title_zh: Worldcoin Rallies As World Chain Value Locked Climbs As Bitcoin Slides Below $85K
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Worldcoin rose over 7% on Saturday, extending a run that has it up roughly 23% over seven days and 61% over a month.
Total value locked on World Chain, the layer-2 network run by the same project, climbed 12.28% over 24 hours, according to DefiLlama data.
The move comes as President Greg Brockman signed for OpenAI instead of CEO Sam Altman, chairman of Tools for Humanity, which makes Worldcoin.
Worldcoin (WLD) edged higher on Saturday, outpacing Bitcoin (BTC) on daily gains as activity on its own blockchain picked up alongside it, as the apex cryptocurrency traded below $85,000.
Total value locked (TVL) on World Chain, which is the Ethereum (ETH) layer-2 network run by the same project behind the WLD token, rose 12.28% over 24 hours to $45.12 million, according to DefiLlama data.
See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox
The token's move extended a longer run, and WLD was up roughly 23% over seven days, 61% over a month, and 25.2% so far this year, or year-to-date (YTD).
Worldcoin was one of the top-trending tickers on Stocktwits. WLD's price was up over 7% during the past 24 hours in comparison to Bitcoin's price which fell over 2%.
On Stocktwits, the retail sentiment around WLD improved to 'extremely bullish' zone from the 'bullish' zone, while chatter around it stayed at 'high' levels over the past day.
Worldcoin's rise in price caught traders who had bet against it. A liquidation happens when a trader borrows to make a leveraged bet, the price moves the wrong way, and the exchange closes the position automatically to stop the losses from growing.
Over the past hour, WLD positions worth about $241,590 were wiped out, against about $133,050 on Bitcoin, according to CoinGlass data. The Worldcoin figure was roughly 82% higher, even though Bitcoin's market cap is significantly larger.
Most of that hour's damage fell on short positions, which are bets that a price will fall. CoinGlass put the hour's total across all tokens at $1.94 million, of which $1.14 million came from shorts.
The longer view was the reverse. Over 24 hours, $343.96 million was liquidated, and $305.45 million of that came from long positions, which are bets that a price will rise. That fits a market where most tokens fell, and Worldcoin was the exception.
WLD trades as an AI-adjacent token, so sentiment around the sector tends to reach it. Worldcoin and its creator, Tools for Humanity, are different firms, but they're linked via their chairman, Sam Altman, the CEO of the AI company, OpenAI (OPEAZZX).
The rally comes on the heels on six executives signed a voluntary AI safety commitment at the White House on Sept. 29, among them Google's (GOOG) Sundar Pichai, Anthropic's Dario Amodei, Meta's (META) Mark Zuckerberg, xAI's Elon Musk, and Nvidia's (NVDA) Jensen Huang.
OpenAI president Greg Brockman signed for his company rather than chief executive Sam Altman, who is chairman of Tools for Humanity, the company behind Worldcoin.
However, on Friday Altman said Cerebras (CRBS) is also a "close partner" of OpenAI, who stated the businesses had a "deep engagement pushing on the frontiers of speed." The transaction includes OpenAI's agreement to use 750 megawatts of Cerebras computing capacity through 2028, with Cerebras stating the arrangement is worth over $20 billion.

articles.title_orig: Avelumab Effective Against Merkel Cell Carcinoma in Real-World Population, Despite Frequent AEs
articles.title_zh: Avelumab Effective Against Merkel Cell Carcinoma in Real-World Population, Despite Frequent AEs
articles.content_orig:
In a real-world cohort of older patients in Austria, avelumab (Bavencio) was determined to be effective for treating Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC), despite frequent adverse events (AEs).
“ Avelumab achieved clinically meaningful outcomes in this older, less-selected routine care cohort,” said first author Magdalena Forstinger, MD, a physician-researcher with Sigmund Freud Privatuniversität and Klinik Hietzing, Vienna. “Adverse events affected treatment in some patients, underscoring the importance of careful monitoring,” she added.
Forstinger presented the findings on October 2 at the European Academy of Dermatology and Venereology (EADV) 2026 Congress in Vienna.
In 2017, avelumab, a programmed death ligand-1 (PD-L1)-blocking antibody, became the first treatment approved by the FDA for MCC. The study abstract noted, however, that evidence of the drug’s efficacy and safety in a routine clinical care context was limited, particularly among older patients, a population more likely to be immunocompromised and have comorbidities, who are underrepresented in trials.
The nationwide, multicenter, retrospective chart review included patients with inoperable locally advanced or metastatic MCC who had received at least one cycle of avelumab, with no other exclusion criteria applied, Forstinger said. A total of 49 patients were included in the study, with a median age of 81 years (range, 62-96). The most common comorbidities were cardiovascular, metabolic, oncologic, and pulmonary.
The primary endpoint was real-world progression-free survival (rwPFS). Secondary endpoints included real-world overall survival (rwOS), objective response rate (rwORR), duration of response (rwDOR), and time to response (rwTTR), and safety.
At the start of treatment, 42.9% of participants had stage IIIB MCC and 57.1% had stage IV MCC. A total of 16.3% were immunocompromised or immunosuppressed, and 77.6% had an ECOG performance status ≤ 1. Avelumab was administered as first-line monotherapy in 77.6% of cases, with 22.4% also receiving other modalities such as radiotherapy. Median follow-up was 8.9 months (range, 0-73.1).
Nearly half of evaluable patients (n=48) responded to avelumab, Forstinger said, and median rwPFS, the primary endpoint, was 10.1 months (95% CI, 1.8-18.4). The rwORR was 47.9% (95% CI, 34.5-61.7), and median rwOS was 22.9 months (95% CI, 5.0-40.8). Median rwTTR was 3.9 months (range, 1.4-12.7), and median rwDOR among responders was 19.2 months (95% CI, 8.9-29.5).
Forstinger observed that rwPFS and rwOS were in a similar range to those reported in the 2021 phase 2 JAVELIN Merkel 200 trial (which evaluated first-line avelumab in patients with metastatic MCC), although rwORR was lower. JAVELIN did not include immunocompromised patients, she added.
Overall, 71.4% of patients experienced an AE and 53.1% experienced an immune- and/or treatment-related AE, including 24.5% who had a grade ≥ 3 AE. AEs led to treatment interruption or discontinuation in 28.6% of participants, including permanent discontinuation in 12.2% of cases.
Previously reported AEs for avelumab in patients with MCC include fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, infusion-related reactions, rash, nausea, constipation , cough, and diarrhea . Potentially serious immune-mediated adverse reactions include pneumonitis, colitis , hepatitis , endocrinopathies, nephritis with renal dysfunction, and dermatologic reactions.
In a post-hoc analysis, scores of ≤ 1 on the ECOG performance status scale, which describes a patient’s level of function, were associated with lower hazard ratios (HRs) for rwPFS (HR, 0.257; 95% CI, 0.100-0.658; P = .005) and rwOS (HR, 0.157; 95% CI, 0.047-0.521; P = .002). Forstinger said these findings should be interpreted as “hypothesis-generating.”
Forstinger has reported no relevant financial relationships.
Scott Harris has covered dermatology for more than a decade. He lives near Washington, DC.

articles.title_orig: MI5 Says China’s MSS Funded Research Involving 100+ U.K.-Linked Academics
articles.title_zh: MI5 Says China’s MSS Funded Research Involving 100+ U.K.-Linked Academics
articles.content_orig:
The U.K.'s domestic intelligence and security agency has warned that more than 100 academics have helped China boost its intelligence gathering efforts on behalf of Beijing's state security service.
In a "Security Service Espionage Alert" issued on September 30, 2026, MI5 said the "primary purpose of the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI) 中国通用技术研究院 is to fund research that directly improves Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS) technical capability for espionage."
CGTRI, also known as the China Academy of General Technology (CAGT), is assessed to be a front company for MSS. The body, per MI5, funds academic research in China on topics including artificial intelligence (AI), cybersecurity, covert communications systems, and steganography.
More than 100 U.K.-linked academics have contributed to research projects funded by MSS via CGTRI, the alert read. In some cases, the individuals may not be aware that CGTRI is providing monetary backing to the Chinese research project they are contributing to.
"This activity supports MSS espionage, which poses a threat to U.K. national security," the unprecedented alert said.
U.K. academic institutions are being urged to immediately review any ongoing or planned collaboration with CGTRI, and trace the funding source when conducting research collaborations with Chinese institutions to ensure that the entity is not involved.
The alert has also cautioned that institutions, staff, and researchers continuing to collaborate could be prosecuted under the National Security Act 2023 for providing material assistance to a foreign intelligence service in carrying out U.K.-related activities.
Responding to the alert, the Chinese embassy in the U.K. called the accusations "imaginary and purely fabricated."
"We firmly oppose such baseless allegations and have lodged solemn representations with the U.K. side," an embassy spokesperson added . "Exchanges and collaboration between U.K. universities and China have always been conducted on a voluntary basis and in compliance with laws and regulations. Such exchanges and collaboration are mutually beneficial."
"We urge the U.K. intelligence authorities to stop spreading falsehoods and stop undermining educational exchanges and research cooperation between China and the U.K."
In August 2025, a report from the U.K.-China Transparency (UKCT) think tank revealed that Chinese students at U.K. universities are being forced to spy on their classmates in an attempt to suppress discussing issues that are sensitive to the Chinese government, an allegation the Chinese embassy has called "groundless and absurd."
"CGTRI [...] has identifiable staffing overlaps with China's University of International Relations, widely known to be uniquely closely affiliated with China's Ministry of State Security," UKCT said . "CGTRI specialises in cybersecurity, signals intelligence, and a variety of AI-enabled tools for strategic national objectives."
"These specialties include capabilities especially useful for conducting cyber-attacks of the kind that Chinese government agencies, including the MSS, have executed against U.K. targets, including companies, universities, and public services and infrastructure."
AI agents are already operating inside enterprises with growing access to sensitive systems and data—while security teams still lack the visibility, controls, and governance to keep that access in check.

articles.title_orig: Doctor Groups Fill In for CDC During Flu Season
articles.title_zh: Doctor Groups Fill In for CDC During Flu Season
articles.content_orig:
SEATTLE — There's a bit of a chill in the air, pumpkin spice in your coffee, and children back to school — which means the threat of respiratory viruses like COVID-19, influenza and RSV is looming.
Some respiratory illnesses have arrived already. Seasonal influenza activity is still low at the national level, data from the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention show.
But certain flu metrics are inching up – especially in the West . Health officials in Washington state's King County note that since mid-August there has been an increase in people with flu visiting emergency departments in the area.
Vaccines that help prevent illness and reduce the risk of serious infections and hospitalization are now available, and for some people, this is the right time to roll up their sleeves.
Typically, the CDC launches a fall campaign around this time of year, recommending seasonal immunizations such as the flu shot and COVID-19 vaccines. But after sweeping changes to the agency's vaccine advisory committee during the second Trump administration and ongoing lawsuits, the CDC recently posted guidance online to follow last year's recommendations for flu and COVID-19.
Meanwhile, the American Medical Association and the University of Minnesota's Vaccine Integrity Project launched their own independent reviews of this fall's vaccines – including those for flu , COVID and RSV – which was published in September in the medical journal JAMA.
The review papers helped inform 2026-27 respiratory virus immunization recommendations released by several medical groups, including the American Academy of Pediatrics, American Academy of Family Physicians, American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists and the Infectious Diseases Society of America.
"For more than 60 years, the United States has benefited from an established federal process for evaluating vaccine evidence and translating that science into recommendations for the American public. At the center of that process were the Centers for Disease Control and its Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices, the ACIP," Dr. Bruce Gellin, board chair of the Vaccine Integrity Project and professor of medicine at Georgetown University, said at a news briefing.
"Unfortunately today, the federal government is not fulfilling that responsibility in the way that it historically has. But the need for that work has not disappeared. Influenza, SARS-CoV-2 and the RSV viruses will circulate again this fall and winter," Gellin said.
"Clinicians will still have patients to care for. Parents will still have decisions to make for their children, and older Americans, pregnant women and people with underlying health conditions will still need to know how best to protect themselves," he said. "We cannot allow the breakdown of a federal process to create a vacuum in evidence-based vaccine guidance."
The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services has not responded to CNN's request for comment on the groups' recommendations.
Flu, COVID-19 and RSV immunizations are now available at most major pharmacies.
"And really reassuringly, insurers have indicated to the major groups that they will cover these respiratory virus immunizations," Dr. Sarah Nosal, president of the American Academy of Family Physicians, said in a news briefing.
Ordering through Vaccines for Children , the federal program that provides routine immunizations at no cost to children who are uninsured or underinsured or whose families may not otherwise be able to afford them, has also started. About half of U.S. children are eligible for the program.
"Vaccines are one of medicine's greatest success stories. They prevent serious illness, reduce hospitalizations and long-term complications and save lives," Nosal said in a news release. "As federal guidance evolves, the science behind vaccines remains strong. These recommendations are grounded in the latest evidence, informed by public health experts and shaped by what family physicians are seeing every day in their patients."
Groups eligible for RSV immunizations include older adults, pregnant people and infants.
"People age 50 and older with high-risk conditions, and everyone over 75 years old, should get one dose," Nosal said. "This is not an annual vaccine. If you got one before, you do not need a new one this year. Getting one should protect you throughout the entire season."
During pregnancy, RSV vaccination is recommended in the third trimester, between weeks 32 and 36.
Children younger than 8 months should be immunized against RSV using a monoclonal antibody unless their mother got an RSV vaccination during pregnancy, said Dr. Andrew Racine, president of the American Academy of Pediatrics.
And a single dose of RSV vaccine is recommended for adults who have weakened immune systems.
For older adults, RSV vaccinations are typically recommended in late summer and early fall.
The advice slightly changed this year for pregnant people.
For infants, the RSV monoclonal antibody is typically recommended around virus season, from October through March.
Everyone 6 months and older is recommended to get an annual flu shot.
"On average, flu vaccines reduce the risk of needing to go to the doctor by 30% to 60%," Nosal said.
"Adults 65 years and older should get an enhanced flu vaccine, one that is high-dose, adjuvanted or recombinant, when it's available," she said. "But do not delay your vaccination if that one's not available."
And for the first time, an mRNA-based flu vaccine is available for use in adults 50 and older.
October is the ideal time to get vaccinated, Nolan said, because "protection wanes throughout the season."
Some providers use the slogan "flu before boo" to remind people to get a flu shot before Halloween.
Getting an updated COVID-19 vaccine is recommended for all adults.
"If you're older than 19, we recommend getting the COVID-19 vaccine," Nosal said.
"This is especially important for people who are 65 years and older, at increased risk for severe COVID infection and those who've never received a COVID-19 vaccine," she said. "For those adults 65 years and older, they should receive a second dose of the updated COVID-19 vaccine six months after that season's initial dose to help maintain protection as immunity wanes over time."
The vaccine is also recommended for infants between six months and 23 months of age, and children in certain high-risk groups or those whose families request vaccination.
It's recommended to get the updated vaccine now, but if you have been recently infected with Covid, experts advise waiting four to six months before getting the vaccine.
The updated COVID-19 vaccine "targets the most recent strain that's been circulating, and so if you want to update your protection, that's the best way to do it," Dr. Sandra Adamson Fryhofer, president-elect of the American Medical Association, said in a news briefing.

articles.title_orig: U.S.-Russia Talks on Ukraine Now Involve an Oil Deal Tied to Trump Allies
articles.title_zh: U.S.-Russia Talks on Ukraine Now Involve an Oil Deal Tied to Trump Allies
articles.content_orig:
The Trump administration's negotiations with Russia over ending the war in Ukraine have expanded into discussions surrounding a multibillion-dollar sale of Russian oil giant Lukoil's international assets, the New York Times reported on Saturday.
The prospective investors of the colossal deal include business figures connected to U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff and President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.
The proposed transaction, which still requires approval from Washington and Moscow, would cover oil fields, refineries, and gas stations around the world.
The leading investment group reportedly includes billionaire Todd Boehly, who has donated $2 million to President Donald Trump's political causes, Qatari and Emirati investors with business connections to Kushner or Witkoff's family, and the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation.
There is no indication that either Witkoff or Kushner personally stands to profit from the transaction.
The negotiations nevertheless highlight the overlap between the administration's diplomacy and the private business relationships surrounding Trump and two of the people participating in his talks with Russia.
The distinction between the two negotiators is significant.
Witkoff holds an official administration position in that The White House identifies him as Trump's special envoy, and he was formally sworn in as senior adviser and special envoy in May 2025.
The administration has repeatedly said he acts under instructions from Trump in diplomatic negotiations.
Kushner, by contrast, does not hold a comparable federal government position.
He is Trump's son-in-law and served as a senior White House adviser during Trump's first term, but the White House has nevertheless included him in high-level diplomatic missions during the second administration.
The White House has also appointed Kushner to Trump's Board of Peace executive board.
Official White House photographs show Kushner traveling alongside Witkoff aboard a U.S. government aircraft and meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Sept. 5 before traveling to Kyiv for talks with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
According to people familiar with the Sept. 5 Kremlin meeting, Putin raised the Lukoil transaction with Witkoff and Kushner and proposed completing it as a demonstration to Russians that economic relations with the United States could resume.
The Americans reportedly agreed to work on the proposal, viewing expanded commercial ties as potentially useful in building goodwill with Moscow and lowering energy prices.
A senior administration official confirmed that Witkoff and Kushner helped negotiate the terms of the federal government's prospective investment, including ''a substantial upfront payment and profits interest for the United States.''
A spokeswoman for Witkoff said he ''takes no salary and travels the world on his own plane, at his own expense, working on behalf of President Trump to negotiate peace and bring hostages home to their families.''
She added that Witkoff ''has no conflict of interest and no financial stake in this matter.''
The DFC similarly defended the prospective investment, saying it ''would advance the Trump administration's commitment to strengthen U.S. economic security, advance U.S. foreign policy, and lower energy prices for everyday Americans.''
The prospective private investors, however, include figures already financially connected to Kushner and the Trump and Witkoff families.
Qatar-based businessmen Moutaz and Ramez Al-Khayyat are expected to hold a major equity stake and are separately working with Kushner and his wife, Ivanka Trump, on financing a multibillion-dollar luxury resort development in Albania.
Another major investor would be an Abu Dhabi fund controlled by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE's national security adviser.
Sheikh Tahnoon controls another fund that purchased a major stake in World Liberty Financial, the Trump family cryptocurrency venture co-founded by Witkoff and now run partly by Witkoff's son.
Sheikh Tahnoon also helps oversee Lunate, an investment fund that is a major stakeholder in Affinity Partners, the private-equity firm Kushner established after leaving government following Trump's first term.
Those relationships have raised questions among ethics specialists about whether private financial relationships could intersect with U.S. foreign-policy decisions.
''This is an alarming and very concerning set of entanglements,'' former Justice Department prosecutor and corporate-compliance lawyer Hui Chen told the Times.
''And it means you have to question how the Trump administration is evaluating the different bidders involved here. Are the personal interests involved going to wrongly influence the outcome?''
The reported connections do not establish that Kushner or Witkoff has manipulated U.S. policy for personal financial benefit.
They do, however, place Kushner, a presidential relative and private investor without Witkoff's formal special-envoy position, in diplomatic negotiations involving foreign businessmen who have concurrent financial relationships with him or members of Trump's family.
The White House itself describes both men as participating in its Russia-Ukraine diplomacy, including the September meetings with Putin and Zelenskyy.
The proposed Lukoil sale ultimately requires Treasury Department approval because the Russian company remains subject to U.S. sanctions.
Asked about Treasury's role, a department spokeswoman said the Office of Foreign Assets Control ''implements foreign policy as determined by the White House.''
The administration sanctioned Lukoil last year as part of an effort to pressure Putin to ''stop the killing,'' forcing the company to seek buyers for its international holdings.
Lukoil has valued its international assets at roughly $20 billion.
Treasury has repeatedly extended licenses permitting portions of the company's international operations to continue while their fate is decided, with the latest extension running through Oct. 29.

The carrier-settings fix will automatically download for AT&T users over the next 14 days, but Apple urged consumers to immediately install any available software updates. Users can manually begin the update by going into the "General" section of the iPhone settings and selecting "About."
For those who have already been affected, the only solution is swapping their phone for a new unit with either Apple or AT&T.
The iPhone 18 Pro Max that's sold in the US differs from other new models in one way: It includes a cellular modem manufactured by Qualcomm Inc. All other versions, including the smaller iPhone 18 Pro, ship with Apple's in-house C2 modem. Only the 18 Pro Max has been affected by the AT&T bug, according to customer reports.

articles.title_orig: Oliver Illini: Real-World Data Highlight the Unmet Need in Second-Line ES-SCLC
articles.title_zh: Oliver Illini: Real-World Data Highlight the Unmet Need in Second-Line ES-SCLC
articles.content_orig:
Oliver Illini , Specialist in Internal Medicine and Pulmonology at Wiener Gesundheitsverbund, shared on LinkedIn :
“Relapsed SCLC is finally moving. But how large was the unmet need just before this therapeutic shift?
Published today in Lung Cancer: our multicenter real-world analysis from four high-volume lung cancer sites in Vienna, conducted as part of the prospective LALUCA registry, provides a snapshot of second-line treatment in ES-SCLC in the chemoimmunotherapy era.
Among 203 patients , only 36.9% proceeded to second-line treatment. Median PFS in second line was 4.7 months, median OS 7.1 months, with treatment still dominated by anthracycline-based regimens, topotecan and platinum rechallenge.
These data may now almost look like a historical benchmark – because the field is changing remarkably fast.
DeLLphi-304 established an OS benefit for tarlatamab, and at WCLC 2026 two randomized phase III trials, TAISHAN-302 and ARTEMIS-008 , independently demonstrated substantial survival improvements with B7-H3-directed ADCs over topotecan.
Cross-trial comparisons are obviously not appropriate, but the direction is difficult to miss. After decades of limited progress, SCLC is finally becoming a genuinely dynamic therapeutic space.
Our data also highlight an important point: improving second-line therapy only helps patients who remain fit enough to reach it. In our cohort, almost two thirds never received a second line.
The next challenge may therefore be not only which drug to use after progression, but how to get more patients to the next effective treatment.
Congratulations to first author Daniel Moser and many thanks to all colleagues and collaborating teams across the Wiener Gesundheitsverbund.

articles.title_orig: Google's Sergey Brin has now donated more than $100 million to oppose California's billionaire tax
articles.title_zh: Google's Sergey Brin has now donated more than $100 million to oppose California's billionaire tax
articles.content_orig:
Google cofounder Sergey Brin has now spent more than nine figures combating California’s proposed wealth tax.
According to filings , Brin donated a total of $102 million to the group Building a Better California, a PAC and political advocacy organization opposing the state’s billionaire tax and supporting other pro-business policies and housing and infrastructure affordability. Campaign filings show efforts to block this tax have exceeding $187 million, making Brin the largest sole contributor to the effort. Contributions supporting the bill have meanwhile reached about $32 million.
Proposition 40 , which will be on the ballot in November, would impose a one-time, 5% tax on California’s 200 billionaires, with 90% of the revenue from the proposed measure going toward the state’s health care program and 10% going toward education, food assistance, and administration. Brin, with a net worth of nearly $260 billion , could owe about $13 billion as a result of the tax.
California, the most populous state, has become the epicenter of the conversation around the K-shaped economy, or the diverging fortunes of those with wealth and those without it. While the Golden State has a $4 trillion GDP, making its economy about the same size as the United Kingdom’s, it also has 18% of its residents living below the poverty line , the highest in the country, in part because of its high cost of living.
The ballot measure has caused an uproar among some of California’s wealthiest individuals such as former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and PayPal cofounder Peter Thiel, both of whom have donated to organizations against the measure. Brin compared the proposal to his socialist Soviet upbringing.
“I fled socialism with my family in 1979 and know the devastating, oppressive society it created in the Soviet Union. I don’t want California to end up in the same place,” he told the New York Times in a statement in April.
California Gov. Gavin Newsom has joined these tech billionaires in combating the measure, arguing the tax would hurt the state by eroding its tax base, ultimately reducing key revenue for social services.
“The fact is it actually will reduce investments in education,” Newsom said in a Bloomberg Businessweek interview earlier this year. “It will reduce investments in teachers and librarians, childcare. It will reduce investments in firefighting and police.”
The opposition to Prop 40 may, in some ways, be a self-fulfilling prophecy, as billionaires including Brin shift business entities out of California in favor of states without similar wealth taxes. Brin now lists Nevada as his residence, according to state records. Larry Page, who cofounded Google alongside Brin, has converted several of his assets out of California, including Koop, his family office, which was incorporated in Delaware in December 2025. Oceankind, an ocean science nonprofit founded by Page’s wife, Lucy Southworth, in 2018 , was similarly incorporated in Delaware around the same time. Brin, for his own part, reportedly bought a $51 million home near Miami Beach in March.
There’s not yet clear evidence to indicate these billionaires’ anxieties about the future of California are well-founded. On one hand, the six billionaires expected to leave California—Brin, Page, Thiel, as well as car loan magnate Don Hankey, former Uber CEO Travis Kalanick, and director Steven Spielberg—would have collectively generated about $27 billion in tax revenue, about one-fourth of the $100 billion the proposal is expected to raise through taxes over five years.
On the other hand, billionaires were already paying so little in California income tax their departure may not pack as much of a punch as anticipated. A working paper published by the National Bureau of Economic Research in May noted billionaires residing in the state paid $4.1 billion in income tax last year, about 0.2% of their collective $2 trillion net worth, meaning that even if every billionaire were to leave the state, it would take about 25 years for lost income tax revenue to cancel out the $100 billion sum California is projected to get from the tax. Even if a billionaire mass exodus included one-quarter of the state’s wealthiest residents, it would take a century to equal the $100 billion windfall.
“The proposed one-off California billionaire tax of 5%, payable over five years, is both small relative to California billionaires’ wealth gains and large relative to the taxes they currently pay,” the authors wrote.

articles.title_orig: A famed Hawaii sea arch collapses, prompting NPS warnings of unstable cliffs
articles.title_zh: A famed Hawaii sea arch collapses, prompting NPS warnings of unstable cliffs
articles.content_orig:
A colossal sea arch that had long been a major landmark on Hawaii’s rugged coastline has collapsed into the Pacific Ocean more than 500 years after it was naturally formed, the local park service confirmed.
Hōlei Sea Arch stood at a height of roughly 90 feet (27 meters) in Hawaii ’s Volcanoes National Park on the southern coast of the Big Island — the largest and youngest island of the Hawaiian chain.
The arch formed around 550 years ago when ancient lava flow from the eruption of one of the island’s six volcanoes hit the cliff edges and carved the vault, creating a natural marvel that drew visitors to the spot for many years, according to the United States National Park Service (NPS).
While the exact time of the collapse is unknown, the Volcanoes National Park team said on social media Thursday that the arch was still standing on Wednesday, September 23, when the park was temporarily closed during Tropical Storm Nolo.
When it reopened on Monday, 28 September, the arch was gone.
“Yes, it’s true. RIP Hōlei Sea Arch,” Volcanoes National Park said in posts of Facebook and Instagram , alongside before-and-after photographs revealing a stark shift in the scenery.
“Hōlei Sea Arch was a very special place to so many of our visitors,” it added.
But the wild and remote coastline’s dramatic transformation had long been expected, according to NPS.
“This formation is beautiful, but temporary, and has a limited life span,” NPS said in a description of the beauty spot on its website.
“The sea arch will eventually crumble into the sea. However, others will replace it as the cliff slowly migrates inland,” it added.
Italy’s famous ‘Lovers’ Arch’ collapses on Valentine’s Day
NPS said the cliff’s lifespan was determined by differential erosion — a process whereby softer rock is worn away faster and harder than stronger, more resistant rock.
Landscapes are routinely reshaped through differential erosion, and it is how the arch came to be more than five centuries ago.
Park staff knew the incessant battering of waves against the sea arch would eventually cause it to crumble into the Pacific, although they were not able to predict exactly when this would happen.
Volcanoes National Park urged visitors to keep their distance from the unstable cliff edges to avoid putting themselves, or first responders, in danger.

articles.title_orig: Europe to release diesel reserves after Trump request
articles.title_zh: Europe to release diesel reserves after Trump request
articles.content_orig:
US President Donald Trump announced on Friday that Europe will release parts of its diesel reserves with immediate effect.
"Europe has just agreed to release a massive amount of their heavily stocked Diesel Oil ," Trump posted on his Truth Social account, adding that the process will begin "immediately."
Trump later hailed the decision as "a great thing."
Speaking about the possibility of a US ban on diesel exports, Trump said such a move "was never really on the table."
The US leader is facing growing pressure at home due to mounting prices of oil and other goods as a result of the Iran war and his trade policies.
According to the American Automobile Association (AAA), the average price of diesel in the US was $6.37 per gallon (€1.496 per liter). Meanwhile, in Germany, the ADAC motoring club said a liter of diesel cost €2.409 ($10.27 per US gallon) on Tuesday, two days before a tax rebate of €0.17 per liter went into effect.
Trump has argued the soaring prices are worth it in order to make sure Iran does not obtain nuclear weapons, with the prices supposedly coming down after the war's end.
Russia's ban on exports, which came due to Ukraine's attacks on its refineries, also contributed to the hit in diesel supply around the world.
French President Emmanuel Macron , who is also the G7 chair, confirmed the news by saying that the G7 will release up to 100 million barrels over the next four months.
Macron also committed to refraining from any trade-limiting measures when it comes to petroleum and energy products between partner countries.
"Our citizens' concerns about energy prices remain a top priority," G7 leaders said in a joint statement published by Macron.
"We will monitor developments closely and stand ready to adjust measures as needed."
This comes after a call between Macron and Trump on the issue overnight, the French Embassy in the US said.
The US had demanded France, Germany and other European countries to release 100 million diesel barrels within a 20-day window, Reuters reported, citing sources.

articles.title_orig: Top Stories: Apple Smart Home Launch on October 13, iPhone Duo Production Issues, and More
articles.title_zh: Top Stories: Apple Smart Home Launch on October 13, iPhone Duo Production Issues, and More
articles.content_orig:
Things are getting crazy in the Apple rumor world, as even though the iPhone 18 Pro and several other products have only just launched and the iPhone Duo is right around the corner, there's even more to come imminently.
October 13 looks to be the date for an introduction of Apple's revamped smart home portfolio, including the home hub device we've been hearing about for ages. This week also saw word that Apple's supply chain is struggling to meet production yield goals for the iPhone Duo ahead of its launch, while iPhone 18 Pro owners are now getting a chance to put the devices through their paces, so read on below for all of the details!
A couple of those leaked products above could be arriving very shortly, as Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman says Apple will be introducing a trio of new smart home products on Tuesday, October 13 .
Apple will reportedly debut its long-rumored smart home hub product, as well as the new HomePod mini and Apple TV models, and while he didn't specify how Apple will introduce them, signs are pointing to some sort of event .
Apple retail stores have reportedly also received confidential boxes that are marked "Do Not Open Until October 8" and which are likely to contain merchandising materials. It's unclear, however, if they are for the upcoming iPhone Duo launch or something related to the smart home product introduction.
Apple's long-rumored smart home hub will have an iMac G4-style design and a host of unique features, Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman reports.
The smart home hub is said to feature a square 6-inch display, with variants that can be placed on a countertop or mounted on a wall. It features a single FaceTime camera on the front, with microphones and speakers in its connected base.
Leaks suggest the hub may be available in Silver, Space Gray, Starlight, and Rose Pink colors , and will be able to display user-customizable Photo Faces pulled from your photos library, memories, and shared albums, a feature that appears similar to what will be available for StandBy mode on the iPhone Duo.
The iPhone Duo is reportedly facing production difficulties ahead of its October launch , with early output expected to be limited.
A person said to be close to Foxconn's supply chain told China's Jiemian News that final assembly yields for Apple's first foldable iPhone were only slightly above 60% as of September 17. The source said that, under Apple's current quality standards, it could take another six months to a year for the assembly line to reach a mature yield.
According to the source, Foxconn is repeatedly adjusting equipment, assembly processes, and production settings as it makes the iPhone Duo at scale. The source also said suppliers were waiting to see whether Apple would ease any quality requirements to accelerate production.
It's been almost two weeks since the iPhone 18 Pro models launched, and we want to hear from MacRumors readers. What do you think of Apple's newest iPhones? If you upgraded from an older phone, was it worth it? What about upgrading from an iPhone 17 Pro? What problems are you running into? Anything you love so far?
MacRumors readers have already been sharing early opinions on the MacRumors forums, and there are interesting discussion threads to read through. For early reviews and hands-on images, make sure to check out the first impressions and photos thread .
Not everything has been perfect, however, as some users have been experiencing issues such as speaker crackling or popping while some iPhone 18 Pro Max users on AT&T in the U.S. have been having issues with cellular connectivity or eSIM provisioning .
John Ternus is marking one month as Apple CEO, and he is apparently undertaking efforts to restructure the company to accelerate product development and introduce new products more frequently , according to Bloomberg 's Mark Gurman.
Ternus apparently wants Apple to "broaden its range of devices and create a leaner organization with a greater focus on engineering." One proposal under consideration is to rely less on Apple's traditional spring and fall product release cycles, and introduce new devices more quickly and throughout the year. Ternus has also purportedly indicated that Apple must become "more experimental" to remain competitive in the era of artificial intelligence.
